classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_pellet
items.description:
Toroidal azimuthal coordinate of a pellet’s center of mass, locating the
pellet around the machine symmetry axis in cylindrical geometry.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the azimuthal position of the pellet center of mass around
the toroidal symmetry axis, expressed as the angle coordinate in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The toroidal coordinate is defined from the horizontal Cartesian coordinates
of the pellet center of mass by

$$
\phi = \operatorname{atan2}(y,x)
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the horizontal Cartesian coordinates in the
right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis, with
$\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$. The coordinate is periodic over one complete toroidal
circuit and identifies the pellet’s azimuthal location, distinct from the
post-shattering [toroidal coordinate of a pellet
fragment](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_pellet_fragment).

The angle uses the same geometric convention as the general [toroidal
angle](name:toroidal_angle), but is evaluated at the pellet center of mass.

Sign convention: Positive when increasing $phi$ follows the direction of
increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$.

items.name: perpendicular_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field
items.description:
Gyro-Bohm-normalized perpendicular momentum flux due to perturbed parallel
magnetic-field fluctuations is the perpendicular velocity-space contribution
to turbulent transport of toroidal angular momentum. Linear forms are
eigenmode weights, while nonlinear forms are turbulent-flux contributions.
items.documentation:
Gyro-Bohm-normalized perpendicular momentum flux due to the perturbed
parallel magnetic field is the perpendicular velocity-space contribution to
turbulent transport of toroidal angular momentum across magnetic flux
surfaces.

The normalized quantity is defined by

$$
\widehat{\Gamma}_{\phi,\perp}^{\delta B_\parallel} = \frac{\Gamma_{\phi,\perp}^{\delta B_\parallel}}{\Gamma_{\mathrm{GB}}}
$$

where the hat denotes gyro-Bohm normalization, $\Gamma_{\phi,\perp}^{\delta
B_\parallel}$ is the toroidal angular-momentum-flux contribution in the
perpendicular velocity-space channel driven by the perturbed parallel
magnetic field, and $\Gamma_{\mathrm{GB}}$ is the gyro-Bohm reference
momentum-flux scale. The subscript $\phi$ identifies toroidal angular
momentum, and $\perp$ identifies the velocity-space channel perpendicular to
the equilibrium magnetic-field direction $\hat{b}$. The perturbation $\delta
B_\parallel$ is the magnetic-field fluctuation along $\hat{b}$, the unit
vector in the direction of the equilibrium magnetic field. The reference
scale follows the gyrokinetic normalization based on [electron density at
the outboard midplane](name:electron_density_at_outboard_midplane) and
[electron temperature at the outboard
midplane](name:electron_temperature_at_outboard_midplane).

For a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, this quantity is expressed as an
eigenmode weight; in nonlinear turbulence, it is the corresponding
turbulent-flux contribution. The quantity does not specify a particular
wavevector summation, time average, or flux-surface average. The
perpendicular designation refers to the velocity-space channel relative to
the equilibrium magnetic field, not to the spatial direction of transport;
the flux is across magnetic flux surfaces.

This is the perpendicular component of the aggregate [normalized momentum
flux due to the perturbed parallel magnetic field], complementary to its
[parallel-channel
contribution](name:parallel_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field).
It isolates the perturbed-parallel-magnetic-field contribution and excludes
electrostatic contributions and the distinct [perpendicular momentum flux
due to the perturbed parallel vector
potential](name:perpendicular_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential).

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal angular-momentum flux is
directed outward across magnetic flux surfaces, away from the magnetic axis.

items.name: toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Signed rate of toroidal angular-momentum transfer per unit volume to bulk
thermal electrons through Coulomb collisions with particles of a specified
distribution.
items.documentation:
Toroidal thermal-electron collisional torque density is the signed
angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered to bulk thermal
electrons through Coulomb collisions with particles of a specified
distribution. It selects one directional component of the collisional
transfer, rather than the full torque-density vector.

Its defining projection is

$$
\tau_{\phi,e,\mathrm{coll}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{coll}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal torque density,
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the [thermal electron
torque-density vector due to
collisions](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions), and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle. The
right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R, \phi, Z)$, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The thermal electrons are the receiving population; this is not the
reciprocal torque acting on the particles of the specified distribution. No
additional orbit-class restriction is imposed, and contributions from
distinct distributions representing the same species are superposed. The
[toroidal co-passing thermal electron torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
restricts the contributing fast-particle distribution to co-passing orbits.
As a component of [torque density](name:torque_density), this quantity is
not a volume-integrated torque and excludes noncollisional contributions.

Sign convention: Positive when the torque-density component delivered to
thermal electrons points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: parallel_neutral_particle_diffusivity
items.description:
Effective parallel particle diffusivity for neutral species, relating
neutral-particle spreading to the local neutral number-density gradient.
items.documentation:
Effective parallel particle diffusivity for neutral species is the
directional transport coefficient that represents neutral-particle spreading
driven by a neutral number-density gradient. It is the parallel
specialization of [neutral particle
diffusivity](name:neutral_particle_diffusivity), with transport resolved
along the magnetic field.

For the field-parallel direction, the diffusive neutral-particle flux is
defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\parallel}\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{n}}}{\partial s_{\parallel}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the parallel diffusive
neutral-particle flux, $D_{\parallel}$ is the parallel neutral particle
diffusivity, $n_{\mathrm{n}}$ is neutral-particle number density, and
$s_{\parallel}$ is physical arclength along the magnetic-field direction.
The minus sign specifies transport down the neutral number-density gradient.

This quantity describes particle transport only; it is distinct from the
parallel energy transport coefficient [parallel neutral energy diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient). Its
directional counterpart is [poloidal neutral particle
diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_diffusivity).

items.name: first_local_tangential_width_of_reflector
items.description:
Full physical extent of a rectangular reflector along its object-local first
tangential axis, defining one dimension of the reflector aperture.
items.documentation:
The first local tangential width of a reflector is the full geometric extent
of an individual rectangular reflector element along its object-local first
tangential axis. It defines one transverse dimension of the reflector
aperture.

For the two bounding edges along this axis, the width is defined as

$$
w_1 = x_{1,\max} - x_{1,\min}
$$

where $w_1$ is the first local tangential width, and $x_{1,\max}$ and
$x_{1,\min}$ are the maximum and minimum signed coordinates of the reflector
edges along the first local tangential axis.

This quantity applies to one reflector member with rectangular geometry. It
is a full width, not a half-width, radius, vertex coordinate, or aggregate
over multiple reflectors; the width is non-negative by the ordering of the
bounding coordinates.

The same full-width convention is used for an aperture's first local
tangential extent in [first local tangential width of
aperture](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_aperture), while [second
local tangential width of
aperture](name:second_local_tangential_width_of_aperture) represents the
corresponding extent along the orthogonal second local tangential axis.

items.name: xenon_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Xenon ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a
plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all positive charge states and
excluding neutral xenon atoms.
items.documentation:
Xenon density at the limiter is the local number density of xenon ions in
the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface.
The evaluation point is the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath
entrance at the plasma-limiter contact, consistent with the parent quantity
[density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter).

When charge states are not individually resolved, this quantity represents
the sum over all positive xenon charge states $\text{Xe}^{q+}$, $q = 1,
\ldots, 54$:

$$
n_{\text{Xe}} = \sum_{q=1}^{54} n_{\text{Xe}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\text{Xe}^{q+}}$ is the number density of xenon in charge state
$q$. Neutral xenon atoms are excluded from this sum.

Xenon is used as a high-$Z$ impurity seed for radiative power exhaust
management in the scrape-off layer. Its concentration at the limiter is set
by the balance of ionization, recombination, and cross-field impurity
transport, and it determines the local particle flux, radiative power load,
and potential sputtering damage to the plasma-facing surface. This quantity
can be inferred from edge emission spectroscopy combined with
collisional-radiative modeling. For xenon impurity density inside the
confined plasma, see [xenon_density](name:xenon_density); for the analogous
quantity at a divertor surface, see
[xenon_density_at_divertor_target](name:xenon_density_at_divertor_target);
and for xenon at the last closed flux surface, see
[xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary).

items.name: temperature_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Energy-equivalent temperature scale at the magnetic axis, representing
either particle thermal energy or radiation brightness.
items.documentation:
Temperature at the magnetic axis is an energy-equivalent measure of a
thermal state or radiation field evaluated at the magnetic axis. It provides
a shared parent concept for kinetic temperatures and brightness
temperatures, which need not represent the same underlying physical state.

For a temperature parameter expressed as an energy-equivalent quantity, the
defining conversion is:

$$
\Theta = k_{\mathrm B} T
$$

where $\Theta$ is the energy-equivalent temperature, $T$ is the underlying
thermodynamic or brightness-temperature parameter, and $k_{\mathrm B}$ is
Boltzmann's constant. This conversion does not imply that a radiation
brightness temperature equals the local kinetic temperature.

The quantity is evaluated at the magnetic axis, the innermost location of
nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces. The parent name specifies no
particle species, charge-state aggregation, radiation band, or
population-weighting convention; it is therefore neither a charge-state sum
nor an all-plasma aggregate by itself.

The [electron temperature at the magnetic
axis](name:electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis) is the kinetic-temperature
specialization for electrons. The [radiative temperature at the magnetic
axis](name:radiative_temperature_at_magnetic_axis) is the
brightness-temperature specialization for electron-cyclotron radiation and
is not necessarily the local kinetic electron temperature. Unlike [plasma
temperature](name:plasma_temperature), this parent does not require an
effective fluid or magnetohydrodynamic aggregation.

items.name: normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal
items.description:
Normalized poloidal flux coordinate locating the pedestal as a linear flux
fraction, referenced to zero at the magnetic axis and one at the last closed
flux surface.
items.documentation:
Normalized poloidal flux coordinate

The coordinate is defined by

$$
\psi_{\mathrm{N}} = \frac{\psi - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}{\psi_{\mathrm{b}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}
$$

where $\psi_{\mathrm{N}}$ is the normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal, $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux on the surface containing the
pedestal location, $\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the [magnetic-axis flux
value](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis), and
$\psi_{\mathrm{b}}$ is the [boundary flux
value](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary) at the last closed
flux surface. The denominator must be nonzero.

The normalization gives zero at the magnetic axis and one at the last closed
flux surface. This quantity uses the linear fraction, not its square root;
it specifies a location rather than a geometric radius, a [pedestal
width](name:pedestal_width), or a spatial average. The [coordinate of the
selected plasma
boundary](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_plasma_boundary)
evaluates the same linear fraction at a different locus.

$$\psi_{\mathrm{N}} = (\psi - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}})/(\psi_{\mathrm{b}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}})$$

items.name: per_toroidal_mode_fast_electron_power_density
items.description:
Volumetric rate of coherent-wave energy absorption by fast, suprathermal
electrons for each toroidal mode number, resolved across a poloidal
cross-section or represented as a flux-surface average.
items.documentation:
Mode-resolved fast-electron absorbed wave power density is the rate at which
coherent-wave energy is absorbed by fast, suprathermal electrons per unit
physical volume for each toroidal mode number.

For a toroidal mode number $n_\phi$, the local mode-resolved power density
is defined as

$$
p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}^{(n_\phi)} = \frac{dP_{e,\mathrm{fast}}^{(n_\phi)}}{dV}
$$

where $p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the mode-resolved fast-electron
power density, $P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the corresponding
[mode-resolved fast-electron absorbed wave
power](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power), $V$ is
physical volume, $n_\phi$ is the toroidal mode number, and the subscripts
$e$ and $\mathrm{fast}$ identify the fast-electron recipient population.

The recipient population is fast, suprathermal electrons; thermal-electron
and ion absorption are distinct contributions. The quantity is specified
separately for each toroidal mode number and may be given locally across a
poloidal cross-section or as a flux-surface average over a magnetic flux
surface.

This is a volumetric absorption rate, not volume-integrated power or
launched wave power. The toroidal mode number identifies the wave harmonic
contributing to absorption, not a Fourier coefficient of the deposited-power
field.

Summing the mode contributions for the same spatial evaluation gives the
[fast-electron absorbed wave power
density](name:fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power_density). Integrating a
mode-resolved density over physical volume gives its corresponding
mode-resolved absorbed wave power. Fast-electron absorption is one recipient
contribution to the [mode-resolved total absorbed wave power
density](name:per_toroidal_mode_total_absorbed_wave_power_density), which
includes other plasma populations.

items.name: normalized_particle_perturbed_current_density
items.description:
Dimensionless vector representing the charge-weighted first velocity moment
of a perturbed particle distribution in a gyrokinetic eigenmode.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the dimensionless particle-frame current response
associated with a perturbed species distribution in a gyrokinetic eigenmode.
It represents the charge-weighted first velocity moment while preserving its
vector character rather than selecting one directional projection.

For species $s$, the normalized particle-current moment is defined by

$$
\mathbf{j}_{s,\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{q_s \int \mathbf{v}\,\delta f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}{J_{\mathrm{ref},s}}
$$

where $q_s$ is the species charge, $\delta f_s$ is its perturbed particle
distribution, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{x}$ is position,
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and $J_{\mathrm{ref},s}$ is the
positive reference current-density scale. The normalization makes
$\mathbf{j}_{s,\mathrm{norm}}$ dimensionless.

The vector can be resolved into directional components; [parallel normalized
particle perturbed current
density](name:parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_current_density) is one
field-aligned member. As a particle-frame moment, it includes the
polarization-drift contribution absent from the corresponding [parallel
normalized gyrocenter perturbed current
density](name:parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density).

items.name: perturbed_plasma_temperature_real_part
items.description:
In-phase component of the complex first-order plasma-temperature
eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier harmonic in linear MHD
stability analysis.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the real, in-phase component of the first-order
plasma-temperature perturbation associated with one toroidal Fourier
harmonic. It is a component of the complex eigenfunction represented by
perturbed plasma temperature.

The in-phase component is defined from the complex perturbation amplitude by

$$
\delta T_{\mathrm{R}} = \operatorname{Re}\!\left(\delta T\right)
$$

where $\delta T_{\mathrm{R}}$ is the real temperature-perturbation component
and $\delta T$ is the full complex first-order temperature eigenfunction.
The result depends on the phase reference chosen for the harmonic and
excludes the quadrature component represented by the imaginary part. It is
not the equilibrium temperature or the complete complex perturbation.

items.name: vertical_outline_of_fiber_optic_current_sensor
items.description:
Signed vertical Z coordinate of a contour point defining the geometric
boundary of a fiber-optic current sensor in the right-handed cylindrical (R,
φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The vertical outline coordinate is the signed height of a point on the
geometric boundary of a fiber-optic current sensor, represented in a
poloidal cross-section. It describes the sensor boundary geometry, not the
sensed current or the optical path.

$$
Z = \mathbf{r} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is the point position relative to the coordinate origin
and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The quantity is geometrically analogous to the contour
coordinate used for [vertical outline of wall
material](name:vertical_outline_of_plasma_facing_component), but applies to
the fiber-optic current sensor boundary.

Sign convention: Positive when the outline point lies in the direction of
increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

items.name: electrostatic_potential_amplitude
items.description:
Normalized phase-independent magnitude of an electrostatic-potential
fluctuation relative to its reference field. It describes amplitude only,
not the signed potential perturbation or its phase.
items.documentation:
Electrostatic potential amplitude is the phase-independent magnitude of a
normalized electrostatic-potential fluctuation about a specified reference
field. It represents the size of the fluctuation in the scalar electrostatic
potential while discarding its sign or complex phase.

The amplitude is defined from the normalized fluctuation as:

$$
A_\Phi = \left|\frac{\Phi_\mathrm{fluc}}{\Phi_\mathrm{norm}}\right|
$$

where $A_\Phi$ is the electrostatic-potential amplitude,
$\Phi_\mathrm{fluc}$ is the electrostatic-potential fluctuation relative to
the chosen reference field, and $\Phi_\mathrm{norm}$ is the potential
normalizing quantity specified for that fluctuation. The vertical bars
denote the modulus; for a real representation they denote absolute value.

This quantity excludes the signed fluctuation, the reference potential
itself, and the complex phase of a fluctuation representation.
Electric-field perturbations require the signed or complex potential
fluctuation; amplitude alone is insufficient to recover sign, phase, or
gradient direction. The [perturbed electrostatic-potential
amplitude](name:perturbed_electrostatic_potential_amplitude) is the
perturbation-specific specialization of this amplitude concept.

items.name: normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate
items.description:
Normalized poloidal flux coordinate labels magnetic surfaces by their
poloidal-flux fraction or its square root, from zero at the magnetic axis to
one at the last closed flux surface.
items.documentation:
Normalized poloidal flux coordinate

The linear normalized poloidal-flux fraction is defined by

$$
\psi_{\mathrm{N}} = \frac{\psi - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}{\psi_{\mathrm{b}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}
$$

where $\psi_{\mathrm{N}}$ is the linear normalized flux fraction, $\psi$ is
the [poloidal magnetic flux of the
surface](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface),
$\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is its [magnetic-axis
value](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis), and
$\psi_{\mathrm{b}}$ is its [boundary
value](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary) at the last closed
flux surface used as the normalization reference. The denominator must be
nonzero.

The square-root parameterization is $\rho_{\mathrm{pol,norm}} =
\sqrt{\psi_{\mathrm{N}}}$, where $\rho_{\mathrm{pol,norm}}$ is the
radius-like normalized poloidal flux coordinate. Both parameterizations
increase from zero at the magnetic axis to one at the last closed flux
surface, but their intermediate values differ. Neither is a geometric
radius, spatial average, or volume integral. Outside the last closed flux
surface, an extension labels flux levels rather than nested closed surfaces;
the square-root form requires a nonnegative flux fraction.

Locus-specific members evaluate the chosen parameterization without changing
its normalization references. The [coordinate at the reflectometer cutoff
position](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_at_reflectometer_cutoff_position)
uses the square-root form. The [coordinate of the selected plasma
boundary](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_plasma_boundary) uses
the linear fraction and can be below one when that selected boundary lies
inside the last closed flux surface.

$$\psi_{\mathrm{N}} = (\psi - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}})/(\psi_{\mathrm{b}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}})$$

items.name: parallel_fast_electron_pressure
items.description:
Pressure of fast electrons parallel to the local magnetic field is the
normal stress from random field-aligned motion of the suprathermal electron
population.
items.documentation:
Pressure of fast electrons parallel to the local magnetic field is the
field-aligned normal component of the nonthermal electron pressure tensor.
It describes random momentum transport along the field without requiring an
isotropic or Maxwellian distribution.

In the nonrelativistic kinetic description, this component is defined by

$$
p_{e,\mathrm{fast},\parallel}=\hat{b}\cdot\mathbf{P}_{e,\mathrm{fast}}\cdot\hat{b}=m_e\int \bigl[(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{e,\mathrm{fast}})\cdot\hat{b}\bigr]^2 f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{e,\mathrm{fast},\parallel}$ is the parallel fast-electron
pressure, $\mathbf{P}_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the [fast-electron pressure
tensor](name:fast_electron_pressure), $m_e$ is the electron mass,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the
local mean velocity of the fast-electron population, $f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$
is its velocity distribution function normalized to its number density, and
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The unit vector
$\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ points along the local magnetic field
$\mathbf{B}$; all quantities are evaluated at the same position and time.

The velocity-space integral includes the entire specified fast-electron
population, not thermal electrons or ions. Subtracting the population's mean
velocity excludes directed bulk-flow momentum flux. This quantity selects
the field-aligned stress rather than the full pressure tensor or its
isotropic trace.

For a gyrotropic distribution, this component and the [perpendicular
fast-electron pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_electron_pressure) are the
two independent normal stresses. They need not be equal; the perpendicular
component is the mean of the two transverse normal stresses, whereas the
parallel component contains only the field-aligned contribution.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude
items.description:
Flux-surface average of the reciprocal square of total magnetic-field
strength, a geometric coefficient in neoclassical and flux-surface-averaged
transport relations.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the flux-surface average of the reciprocal square of the
total magnetic-field strength on a nested magnetic surface. It captures
field-strength geometry independently of the magnetic-field direction.

The defining relation is

$$
\left\langle \frac{1}{|\mathbf{B}|^2} \right\rangle_\psi
=
\frac{\displaystyle \int_{S(\psi)} |\mathbf{B}|^{-2}\,\frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}
{\displaystyle \int_{S(\psi)} \frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}$ is the total magnetic-field vector, $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its
magnitude, $\psi$ is the flux-surface label, $S(\psi)$ is the magnetic
surface labeled by $\psi$, $dS$ is its surface-area element, and
$\nabla\psi$ is the spatial gradient of the flux-surface label.

The quantity applies to the complete magnetic flux surface and uses the
inverse-$|\nabla\psi|$ weighting shown in the defining relation. It is not a
pointwise inverse-square field value and has no selection by magnetic-field
direction, component, species, or source.

It is the flux-surface-averaged transformation of the parent [inverse square
of magnetic-field
magnitude](name:inverse_of_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude), with the
reciprocal square formed locally before averaging. It is distinct from
[flux-surface-averaged magnetic-field
magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_magnetic_field_magnitude) and
[flux-surface-averaged square of magnetic-field
magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude),
because nonlinear inversion and squaring do not commute with surface
averaging.

items.name: radiated_power_over_core_region
items.description:
Radiated power over the core region is the electromagnetic energy emitted
per unit time, summed over all emitting plasma species and the full photon
spectrum.
items.documentation:
Radiated power over the core region is the total rate at which plasma in
that region emits energy as electromagnetic radiation. It is integrated over
the region's emitting volume.

The defining volume integral is

$$
P = \int_{V_{\rm core}} p_{\rm rad}\,dV
$$

where $P$ is the radiated power over the core region, $V_{\rm core}$ is the
integration volume, $p_{\rm rad}$ is the local [radiated power
density](name:radiated_power_density), and $dV$ is a volume element.

The quantity sums contributions from all emitting plasma species and charge
states over the full photon spectrum and all emission directions. It
excludes radiation emitted outside the core region and nonradiative
conductive and convective energy transport.

It is the core-region contribution to [total plasma radiated
power](name:total_plasma_radiated_power), whose spatial integral covers the
entire emitting plasma volume. The [core-region power due to impurity
radiation](name:radiated_power_over_core_region_due_to_impurity_radiation)
is only the impurity-radiation component, not the full quantity.

items.name: toroidal_ion_momentum_flux
items.description:
Toroidal ion momentum flux is the area-averaged transport of toroidal linear
momentum across a magnetic flux surface for one ion species, summed over
ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Toroidal ion momentum flux describes transport of the toroidally directed
component of linear [momentum](name:momentum) across a magnetic flux
surface. Toroidal specifies the transported momentum component, not the
direction in which that momentum crosses the surface.

The surface-area-averaged flux is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{i,\phi} = \frac{1}{A_\rho}\int_{S_\rho} \hat{\phi}\cdot\mathsf{T}_i\cdot\hat{n}_\rho\,dA
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\phi}$ is this toroidal ion momentum flux, $i$ identifies
the selected ion species, $S_\rho$ is the magnetic flux surface labeled by
the outward-increasing flux label $\rho$, $A_\rho$ is its total area, $dA$
is a surface-area element, and $\hat{n}_\rho$ is its outward unit normal.
The tensor $\mathsf{T}_i$ is the selected species' linear-momentum flux
tensor, summed over ionic charge states, with its first index denoting the
momentum component and its second the transport direction. The unit vector
$\hat{\phi}$ points along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and
$Z$ is vertical height.

The flux includes convective transport and pressure, viscous, or turbulent
stress contributions; it is not restricted to diffusive transport. It
applies to one ion species and excludes neutrals and other ion species.
Summing the corresponding [charge-state-resolved
fluxes](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) over all ionic charge
states gives this species-level flux. Summing over ion species gives the
toroidal component of the total [ion momentum flux](name:ion_momentum_flux).

This quantity is a flux per unit surface area, not a surface-integrated
transport rate. It transports linear momentum rather than angular momentum
and is distinct from the local angular-momentum source represented by
[toroidal ion torque density](name:toroidal_ion_torque_density).

Sign convention: Positive when the net transport carries momentum directed
along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ outward, or oppositely directed
momentum inward.

items.name: co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Torque density vector giving the angular-momentum source per unit volume
deposited by Coulomb collisions on co-passing fast ions in a specified
charge state.
items.documentation:
The collisional torque density vector for co-passing fast ions in charge
state $q$ quantifies the angular-momentum source per unit volume arising
from Coulomb collisions of those ions with background plasma particles.
Co-passing fast ions are suprathermal ions whose guiding-center orbits
circulate continuously around the torus in the same direction as the plasma
current.

The quantity is the first angular-momentum moment of the Coulomb collision
operator restricted to the co-passing phase-space domain
$\Omega_\mathrm{co}$:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{q,\mathrm{co}} = m_i \int_{\Omega_\mathrm{co}} (\mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{v})\, C[f_q]\, d^3v
$$

where $m_i$ is the fast-ion mass, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector,
$\mathbf{v}$ is the particle velocity, $C[f_q]$ is the Coulomb collision
operator acting on the fast-ion distribution function $f_q$ for ions in
charge state $q$, and $\Omega_\mathrm{co}$ is the co-passing region of phase
space.

This quantity is the co-passing orbit-class contribution to the
charge-state-resolved fast-ion collisional torque density
[fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
excluding trapped and counter-passing populations. Its toroidal projection
is
[toroidal_co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
The orbit-integrated counterpart without charge-state resolution is
co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions.

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal angular-momentum source acts in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: ion_charge_state_energy_flux
items.description:
Ion charge-state energy flux is the net conductive and convective energy
transport per unit area and time in a specified direction for one ion
species and charge state.
items.documentation:
Ion charge-state energy flux is the signed net energy transported through an
oriented surface per unit area and time by ions of one species in one
specified charge state. It includes conductive and convective contributions
to that population's energy transport.

The local directional flux is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{i,z}^{(\hat{\mathbf n})} = \frac{\partial^2 W_{i,z}^{\mathrm{cross}}}{\partial A\,\partial t} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{i,z}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}
$$

where $i$ identifies the ion species, $z$ identifies its charge state,
$\Gamma_{i,z}^{(\hat{\mathbf n})}$ is the directional energy flux,
$W_{i,z}^{\mathrm{cross}}$ is the cumulative net energy carried across the
surface patch by those ions, $A$ is the patch area, $t$ is time,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{i,z}$ is their energy-flux-density vector, and
$\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the selected positive unit normal.

This quantity is not summed over ion species or charge states and excludes
energy carried by electrons or neutrals. It is a signed projection, not a
vector magnitude or surface-integrated power. Unlike the [ion charge-state
energy diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient), it
represents transported energy rather than a coefficient relating the
diffusive contribution to a temperature gradient.

No particular surface orientation is fixed by this parent definition. The
[radial component](name:radial_ion_charge_state_energy_flux) selects the
major-radius direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height. The [parallel
component](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_flux) instead selects the
local magnetic-field direction. Summing the charge-state-resolved fluxes
over all ion species and charge states, using the same projection direction,
gives the corresponding component of [total ion energy
flux](name:total_ion_energy_flux).

Sign convention: Positive when net energy transport by the specified ions
crosses the surface in the selected direction $\hat{\mathbf n}$.

items.name: neutral_power_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Net rate of energy deposited on one divertor target by incident neutral
particles, including charge-exchange neutrals and neutral products of volume
recombination.
items.documentation:
Neutral-particle target power is the rate at which neutral atoms or
molecules transfer energy to one specified divertor target through
bombardment from the plasma. It includes neutrals formed by charge exchange
and volume recombination, and is distinct from the charged-particle target
power [power at divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target).

$$
P_{\mathrm{n,t}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{t}}} \mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{n}}^{\mathrm{net}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{p\to t}}\, dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{n,t}}$ is the deposited neutral-particle power,
$A_{\mathrm{t}}$ is the surface area of the specified target,
$\mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{n}}^{\mathrm{net}}$ is the net neutral energy-flux
vector crossing that surface, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{p\to t}}$
points from the plasma toward the target material.

The quantity excludes charged-particle sheath power, radiative absorption,
and conductive power. Summing the corresponding contributions over all
wetted divertor surfaces gives [neutral power of
divertor](name:neutral_power_of_divertor); recombination-only contributions
are covered by [power at divertor target due to
recombination](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination).

items.name: outer_squareness_of_flux_surface
items.description:
Dimensionless Luce shape coefficient for the outboard corners of nested
magnetic flux surfaces, measuring signed departure from a co-centered
reference ellipse across upper and lower quadrants.
items.documentation:
The outer squareness of a flux surface is the dimensionless Luce (2013)
shape coefficient that characterizes how much the outboard (larger major
radius) corners of a nested toroidal magnetic flux surface depart from a
reference ellipse sharing the same center, horizontal half-width, and
[elongation](name:elongation_of_flux_surface). It is the outboard
counterpart within the
[squareness_of_flux_surface](name:squareness_of_flux_surface) family,
complementing the [inner squareness](name:inner_squareness_of_flux_surface),
and abstracts over the quadrant-resolved coefficients [upper outer
squareness](name:upper_outer_squareness_of_flux_surface) and [lower outer
squareness](name:lower_outer_squareness_of_flux_surface).

At the modeled outboard corners, the reference condition is

$$
\zeta_{\rm out}=0 \Longleftrightarrow \mathcal{C}_{\rm out}=\mathcal{E}_{\rm out}
$$

where $\zeta_{\rm out}$ is the outer squareness coefficient,
$\mathcal{C}_{\rm out}$ is the modeled outboard corner of the flux-surface
cross-section, and $\mathcal{E}_{\rm out}$ is the corresponding reference
ellipse. The cross-section is described in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity does not select either the upper or lower outboard quadrant;
those quadrant-specific coefficients may differ for an up-down asymmetric
flux surface. Positive values describe boxier outward corners, while
negative values describe corners indented relative to the reference ellipse.

items.name: requested_voltage_of_spectrometer_channel
items.description:
Commanded detector-bias potential difference applied by the high-voltage
supply associated with one spectrometer channel.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the requested electrical potential difference that
establishes the detector-bias setpoint for one spectrometer channel.

The setpoint is defined by

$$
V_{\mathrm{set}} = V_{\mathrm{bias}} - V_{\mathrm{return}}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{set}}$ is the requested channel bias voltage,
$V_{\mathrm{bias}}$ is the electrical potential of the high-voltage bias
terminal, and $V_{\mathrm{return}}$ is the electrical potential of the
associated supply return.

The quantity applies to one spectrometer channel and represents a commanded
setpoint rather than an aggregated value across channels. It specifies the
intended bias potential of the channel's high-voltage supply; it does not
represent the channel's actual electrical output signal, which is described
by [voltage of a spectrometer
channel](name:voltage_of_spectrometer_channel).

As a requested control quantity, it is distinct from the realized or
measured channel voltage and is analogous in semantic role to the bias
setpoint represented by [requested voltage of a neutron
detector](name:requested_voltage_of_neutron_detector).

items.name: poloidal_angle_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode
items.description:
The geometric poloidal angle coordinate associated with a gyrokinetic
eigenmode, measured about the flux-surface cross-section center from the
low-field-side midplane.
items.documentation:
This geometric coordinate labels position around the poloidal cross-section
associated with a gyrokinetic eigenmode. It expresses poloidal variation of
equilibrium and eigenmode quantities and refines the general [poloidal
angle](name:poloidal_angle_of_flux_surface) concept for the eigenmode
coordinate.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the angle is defined
relative to the geometric center $(R_0,Z_0)$ of the flux-surface
cross-section:

$$
\theta = \operatorname{wrap}_{[-\pi,\pi]}\left[-\operatorname{atan2}(Z-Z_0,R-R_0)\right]
$$

where $R$ is major radius, $Z$ is vertical height, $R_0$ and $Z_0$ are the
center coordinates, and `wrap` selects the representative angle in the
stated interval. The coordinate is geometric rather than a coil-orientation
parameter or a straight-field-line angle.

Sign convention: Positive when moving clockwise from the low-field-side
midplane in the poloidal cross-section.

items.name: wave_power
items.description:
Rate at which electromagnetic-wave energy is transferred to a selected
plasma particle population or charge state.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the net electromagnetic-wave power absorbed by plasma
particles, representing energy transfer from the wave field to a selected
population or charge state.

$$
P_{\rm abs} = \left.\frac{dE_{\rm particles}}{dt}\right|_{\rm waves}
$$

where $P_{\rm abs}$ is absorbed wave power and $E_{\rm particles}$ is the
energy of the selected particle population; the subscript indicates that
only energy transfer caused by the electromagnetic wave is included.

The quantity excludes launched or generator power, unabsorbed wave power,
and energy merely transported by the wave. Spatially cumulative instances,
such as [ion charge-state power inside a flux
surface](name:ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface), apply this
definition to a specified enclosed plasma volume.

items.name: poloidal_magnetic_field_at_pedestal_top_high_field_side
items.description:
Poloidal magnetic field at the high-field-side pedestal top is the magnitude
of the equilibrium magnetic-field projection onto the poloidal plane.
items.documentation:
Poloidal magnetic field at the high-field-side pedestal top is the local
strength of the poloidal-plane projection of the equilibrium [magnetic
field](name:magnetic_field).

The field strength is defined by

$$
B_{\mathrm{p}} = \sqrt{B_R^2 + B_Z^2}
$$

where $B_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude, and $B_R$
and $B_Z$ are the radial and vertical magnetic-field components, all
evaluated at the stated locus. These components refer to the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The toroidal contribution is excluded, distinguishing this quantity from the
magnitude of the [total magnetic field at the same
locus](name:magnetic_field_at_pedestal_top_high_field_side). This is a local
value, not the [flux-surface-averaged poloidal magnetic field at the
pedestal
top](name:flux_surface_averaged_poloidal_magnetic_field_at_pedestal_top).
The [low-field-side
counterpart](name:poloidal_magnetic_field_at_pedestal_top_low_field_side)
evaluates the same component magnitude at its separately specified locus.

items.name: parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Parallel Pfirsch–Schlüter current density due to diamagnetic drift is the
signed field-aligned return current balancing the divergence of
pressure-gradient-driven perpendicular current in magnetized edge plasma.
items.documentation:
Parallel Pfirsch–Schlüter current density due to diamagnetic drift is the
signed field-aligned return-current contribution to [electric current
density](name:current_density) in magnetized edge plasma. It maintains
current continuity by balancing the divergence of the
pressure-gradient-driven perpendicular diamagnetic current.

The field-aligned projection is defined by

$$
j_{\parallel,\mathrm{PS,dia}}=\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{PS,dia}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}, \qquad \hat{\mathbf{b}}=\frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{PS,dia}}$ is the parallel Pfirsch–Schlüter
diamagnetic-return-current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{PS,dia}}$ is its
field-aligned current-density vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local
magnetic-field vector, $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along that field.

In the quasineutral current-continuity balance, this contribution satisfies
$\nabla\cdot(j_{\parallel,\mathrm{PS,dia}}\hat{\mathbf{b}})=-\nabla\cdot\mathbf{j}_{\perp,\mathrm{dia}}$,
where $\mathbf{j}_{\perp,\mathrm{dia}}$ is the perpendicular
diamagnetic-current-density vector and $\nabla\cdot$ denotes spatial
divergence. The quantity is local, without flux-surface averaging, and
excludes the perpendicular diamagnetic current itself and unrelated
parallel-current contributions.

The parent [Pfirsch–Schlüter current density due to diamagnetic
drift](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is
intrinsically field-aligned, so the explicit parallel projection preserves
its signed amplitude rather than introducing a distinct mechanism. This is
the Pfirsch–Schlüter return-current contribution within [parallel current
density due to diamagnetic
drift](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), not the
total parallel plasma current.

Sign convention: Positive when the Pfirsch–Schlüter diamagnetic return
current flows in the direction of the local magnetic-field unit vector
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

items.name: twist_period_of_fiber_optic_current_sensor
items.description:
Repeat arclength along the sensing-fiber centerline at which the effective
birefringent-axis orientation completes one spatial cycle.
items.documentation:
The twist period is the repeat arclength along the sensing-fiber centerline
for the effective birefringent-axis orientation to return to the same state.

Let $s$ denote arclength along the fiber centerline and $Q(s)$ denote the
specified effective birefringent-axis state. The twist period $L_{\rm tw}$
is defined by

$$
Q(s + L_{\rm tw}) = Q(s)
$$

where $L_{\rm tw}$ is the smallest positive repeat arclength.

This is the twist-specific member of the fiber optic current sensor period.
It describes spatial repetition of the optical anisotropy, not the total
fiber arclength, the [initial twist
phase](name:initial_spun_twist_phase_of_fiber_optic_current_sensor), or the
polarization beat length.

items.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface
items.description:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by a specified thermal ion charge state
within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by a specified thermal ion charge state
within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface. It
is the portion of wave power transferred to thermal ions in that charge
state, accumulated over the volume inside the chosen surface.

The cumulative power is defined by integrating the local absorbed-wave-power
density for that thermal ion charge state over the enclosed plasma volume:

$$
P_q^{\mathrm{th}}(\lambda) = \int_{V(\lambda)} p_q^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x}) \, dV
$$

where $P_q^{\mathrm{th}}(\lambda)$ is the cumulative absorbed wave power for
thermal ion charge state $q$ inside the magnetic flux surface labeled by
$\lambda$, $p_q^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local absorbed-wave-power density for
that thermal ion charge state, and $V(\lambda)$ is the plasma volume
enclosed by that magnetic flux surface.

This quantity is charge-state resolved and includes only absorption by the
thermal ion population; it excludes absorption by electrons, fast or
non-thermal ions, neutrals, and non-wave power exchange. Because power is
extensive, the sum over all thermal-ion charge states gives
[thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface).
It is the thermal-population contribution to
[ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface);
the corresponding fast-ion contribution is
[fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

items.name: krypton_prefill_count
items.description:
Krypton prefill count is the total amount of neutral krypton introduced
before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 36
count units per atom.
items.documentation:
Krypton prefill count is the total amount of neutral krypton (Kr) introduced
during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. Each neutral krypton atom contributes 36
equivalent electrons.

The equivalent-electron count is obtained by accumulating the injected
krypton atoms over the prefill interval and weighting them by the krypton
atomic number:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} N_{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} \int_{t_0}^{t_\mathrm{bd}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}(t)\,dt = 36 \int_{t_0}^{t_\mathrm{bd}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}}$ is the dimensionless
equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}}$ is the dimensionless
accumulated neutral-krypton atom count, $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}=36$ is the
dimensionless atomic number of krypton, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the
neutral-krypton atom injection rate, $t_0$ is the start of prefill, and
$t_\mathrm{bd}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity includes only krypton introduced before breakdown and excludes
later fueling, other gas species, and the retained or ionized inventory. It
uses the common equivalent-electron bookkeeping of
[prefill_count](name:prefill_count), with xenon_prefill_count providing the
analogous noble-gas convention for xenon.

items.name: electron_density_at_pedestal_maximum
items.description:
Electron density at pedestal maximum is the electron number density
evaluated at the pedestal maximum, the steep mid-pedestal location of
maximum pedestal-gradient magnitude. It is the density value at that locus,
not the slope with respect to normalized poloidal-flux coordinate.
items.documentation:
Electron density at pedestal maximum is the electron number density
evaluated at the pedestal maximum, the steep mid-pedestal locus whose
position is given by the [normalized poloidal-flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is a
local density value of the electron population at that flux-coordinate
position.

The defining evaluation is

$$
n_{e,\mathrm{ped,max}} = n_e(\psi_{N,\mathrm{ped}})
$$

where $n_{e,\mathrm{ped,max}}$ is the electron density at pedestal maximum,
$n_e(\psi_N)$ is the [electron density](name:electron_density) as a function
of normalized poloidal-flux coordinate $\psi_N$, and $\psi_{N,\mathrm{ped}}$
is the [normalized poloidal-flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal).

The scope is the free-electron population in the pedestal region at this
single locus. The value is local rather than averaged over the pedestal or
integrated over a flux surface or volume, and no ion charge-state
aggregation is part of this electron quantity.

It is distinct from the pedestal-top electron density and from a maximum
value of $n_e$ over the pedestal; the word maximum denotes the
pedestal-gradient locus, not an extremum of electron density. It is also
distinct from the signed gradient or slope of electron density with respect
to $\psi_N$.

The associated derivative of electron density at pedestal maximum with
respect to normalized poloidal-flux coordinate is $\partial n_e/\partial
\psi_N$ evaluated at the same pedestal maximum locus; that derivative
characterizes the local gradient, whereas $n_{e,\mathrm{ped,max}}$ is the
value being differentiated.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_major_radius
items.description:
Flux-surface average of reciprocal major radius, providing a geometric
equilibrium coefficient for toroidal geometry in flux-coordinate equations.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the geometric average of the reciprocal major radius over a
complete magnetic flux surface. It is an equilibrium metric coefficient
independent of plasma species, population, magnetic-field component, and
physical transport process.

For a magnetic flux surface identified by the label $\psi$, the defining
flux-surface average is:

$$
g_{1/R}(\psi) =
\left\langle \frac{1}{R} \right\rangle_\psi =
\frac{\displaystyle\oint_{\mathcal{S}(\psi)}
\frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}\,\frac{1}{R}}
{\displaystyle\oint_{\mathcal{S}(\psi)}
\frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}
$$

Here $g_{1/R}$ denotes the metric coefficient, $R$ is the major-radius
coordinate, $\psi$ is the magnetic flux-surface label, $\mathcal{S}(\psi)$
is the corresponding closed magnetic flux surface, $dS$ is its surface-area
element, and $\nabla\psi$ is the spatial gradient of the flux-surface label.
The coordinate $R$ belongs to the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, where $\phi$ is the toroidal angle and $Z$ is the vertical
coordinate.

The aggregation is over the entire closed flux surface using the
flux-surface weighting shown in the defining relation; this is not the local
reciprocal radius at a point. The quantity is distinct from the flux-surface
average of reciprocal squared major radius, [flux-surface-averaged inverse
square of major
radius](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_square_of_major_radius).

It is the flux-surface-averaged specialization of [inverse major
radius](name:inverse_of_major_radius): the averaging operator is applied to
the local reciprocal-major-radius quantity without introducing a species,
field-component, or process restriction.

items.name: area_of_first_wall
items.description:
Total geometric area of the material surface forming the plasma-facing first
wall, including installed wall armor and bare vessel surface where
applicable.
items.documentation:
The first-wall area is the geometric measure of the material surface exposed
toward the plasma and forming the innermost plasma-facing boundary. It
includes installed wall armor and bare vessel surface where no armor is
present, but excludes backing structures and surfaces that are not
plasma-facing.

$$
A_{\mathrm{FW}} = \int_{\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{FW}}} \mathrm{d}A
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{FW}}$ is the total first-wall area,
$\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{FW}}$ is the plasma-facing first-wall surface, and
$\mathrm{d}A$ is an elemental surface area. This surface measure is distinct
from the enclosed [volume of the first wall](name:volume_of_first_wall) and
provides the geometric basis for integrating areal loads such as energy flux
at the wall.

items.name: parallel_total_current_density
items.description:
Parallel total current density is the flux-surface average of the total
current–magnetic-field dot product divided by the reference vacuum toroidal
field.
items.documentation:
Parallel total current density represents the net field-aligned conventional
charge flow using a magnetic-field-weighted flux-surface average and a
reference vacuum toroidal field. It is the parallel-basis member of [total
current density](name:total_current_density), rather than the full
current-density vector.

The defining relation is:

$$
j_\parallel = \frac{\left\langle \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}}\cdot\mathbf{B}\right\rangle}{B_0}
$$

where $j_\parallel$ is the parallel total current density,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the net plasma [current-density
vector](name:current_density), $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field
vector, angle brackets denote a normalized flux-surface average, and $B_0$
is the signed reference vacuum toroidal magnetic field at the specified
reference major radius. The reference field must be nonzero.

The total is the algebraic sum over all included charged species and charge
states. It includes ohmic current and non-inductive current, with bootstrap
and externally driven currents included within the non-inductive
contribution. Every contribution uses the same averaging and reference-field
convention. This quantity is neither a current magnitude nor, in general,
the local field-aligned projection or its unweighted flux-surface average.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Unlike [vertical total
current density](name:vertical_total_current_density), which resolves charge
flow along the vertical direction, this quantity resolves the
magnetic-field-aligned contribution; it is also distinct from the toroidal
projection.

Sign convention: Positive when the flux-surface-averaged total
current–magnetic-field dot product and $B_0$ have the same sign; $B_0$ is
positive in the direction of increasing $\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description:
Signed toroidal projection of an effective E×B fluid drift assigned to one
neutral species in a specified internal state.
items.documentation:
The toroidal component of the [effective neutral internal-state E×B drift
velocity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift)
is its signed projection along the geometric toroidal direction. This
direction follows increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For the assigned ideal E×B drift, the defining projection is

$$
v^0_{E,\phi} = \mathbf{v}^0_E \cdot \hat{\phi} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\phi}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}.
$$

Here $v^0_{E,\phi}$ is the effective toroidal drift component for the
specified neutral internal state, $\mathbf{v}^0_E$ is its assigned ideal E×B
drift velocity, $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is
the local magnetic field, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward
increasing toroidal angle. The superscript $0$ labels the neutral
population. The definition requires a nonzero magnetic field.

This quantity applies locally to one specified internal state of one neutral
species in the edge plasma; it is neither summed nor averaged over internal
states or species. It denotes an effective fluid-velocity contribution, not
a direct charged-particle guiding-center drift of electrically neutral
particles. Other contributions to neutral motion are excluded. It is a
linear velocity component, not a toroidal angle or angular velocity.

Unlike the [parallel
component](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift),
which vanishes identically for the assigned ideal E×B drift, the toroidal
projection need not vanish: the geometric toroidal direction is not
generally aligned with the local magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when the assigned E×B velocity has a component in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: radial_electron_particle_flux
items.description:
Radial electron particle flux is the signed net electron-number transport
across magnetic flux surfaces per unit area normal to a surface. It includes
diffusive and convective contributions to electron-density transport.
items.documentation:
Radial electron particle flux is the signed net transport of electron number
across magnetic flux surfaces, per unit area normal to a surface. It is the
flux-surface-normal component of [electron particle
flux](name:electron_particle_flux); crossings in opposite directions
contribute with opposite signs.

The flux-surface-normal component is defined by projection:

$$
\Gamma_{e,\rho} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e \cdot \hat{\mathbf n}_\rho
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,\rho}$ is this flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e$ is the
electron particle-flux vector, $\hat{\mathbf n}_\rho$ is the unit normal to
a surface of constant $\rho$ oriented toward increasing $\rho$, and the
subscript $e$ identifies electrons. The flux coordinates
$(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ label magnetic surfaces and specify position on them,
with $\rho$ the radial flux label, $\theta$ the poloidal angle, and $\phi$
the toroidal angle.

The quantity applies to the electron population in plasma and includes both
diffusive and convective contributions. It is a local per-area particle
flux, not a surface-integrated rate, electron energy flux, or
electric-current density.

In the electron-density transport balance, this total flux contributes to
the evolution of [electron density](name:electron_density) through radial
transport; it is not itself a source or sink. Its convective contribution is
the product of electron density and [radial electron convection
velocity](name:radial_electron_convection_velocity).

Sign convention: Positive when the net electron particle flow crosses a
surface of constant $\rho$ toward increasing $\rho$.

items.name: vertical_ion_momentum_flux
items.description:
Vertical ion momentum flux is the transport rate per unit area of the
vertical component of linear momentum for the total ion population through a
surface whose normal is parallel to the Z direction in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, summed over all ion species and charge states.
items.documentation:
Vertical ion momentum flux is the transport rate per unit area of the
vertical component of linear momentum for the total ion population through a
surface whose normal is parallel to the $Z$ direction in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $Z$ is vertical height, summed over
all ion species and charge states. It is the $Z$-momentum, $Z$-normal
projection of the total [ion momentum flux](name:ion_momentum_flux),
including convective, scalar-pressure, and viscous or turbulent stress
contributions.

The $ZZ$ component of the ion momentum-flux tensor gives this quantity:

$$
\Pi_{\mathrm{ion},ZZ} = \hat{\mathbf{Z}} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_\mathrm{ion} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{Z}} = \sum_s \left( m_s n_s v_{s,Z}^2 + p_s + \pi_{s,ZZ} \right)
$$

where $\Pi_{\mathrm{ion},ZZ}$ is the vertical ion momentum flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}_\mathrm{ion}$ is the [ion momentum
flux](name:ion_momentum_flux) tensor, $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the unit vector
in the direction of increasing vertical height $Z$, $m_s$ is the ion mass of
population $s$, $n_s$ is its number density, $v_{s,Z}$ is its vertical
mean-fluid velocity component, $p_s$ is its scalar pressure, and
$\pi_{s,ZZ}$ is its viscous or turbulent stress component, with the sum
running over all ion species and charge states.

This quantity is the total-ion, charge-state-summed counterpart of the
charge-state-resolved [vertical ion charge-state momentum
flux](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux). It differs from
[toroidal ion momentum flux](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_flux), [poloidal ion
momentum flux](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux), and [parallel ion momentum
flux](name:parallel_ion_momentum_flux) by resolving both the transported
momentum component and the surface-normal direction along $Z$ rather than
along toroidal, poloidal, field-aligned, or flux-surface-normal projections.

Sign convention: Positive when ion linear momentum in the
$+\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame is transported across a surface whose normal points in the
$+\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ direction.

items.name: plasma_temperature_imaginary_part
items.description:
Imaginary part of plasma temperature is the quadrature component of a
complex-valued plasma-temperature quantity. It is the coefficient of the
imaginary basis element and is distinct from both the real part and the full
complex temperature.
items.documentation:
Imaginary part of plasma temperature is the scalar component multiplying the
imaginary basis element in a complex representation of a plasma-temperature
quantity. It represents the quadrature component relative to the chosen
complex phase reference, such as the phase used for a harmonic perturbation
or eigenfunction.

For a complex plasma-temperature quantity $T_c$, the decomposition is

$$
T_c = T_R + i T_I
$$

where $T_c$ is the complex plasma temperature, $T_R$ is the real part of
that quantity, $T_I$ is the imaginary part of plasma temperature, and $i$ is
the imaginary unit.

This quantity is not the full complex plasma temperature and does not
include the real component. The specialization [perturbed plasma temperature
imaginary part](name:perturbed_plasma_temperature_imaginary_part) applies
this same imaginary-part concept to a first-order plasma-temperature
perturbation.

Sign convention: Positive when the coefficient of $+i$ in the chosen complex
representation of the plasma temperature is positive.

items.name: thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Signed local rate of Coulomb-collisional energy transfer from nonthermal
particles to bulk thermal electrons, including all nonthermal guiding-center
orbit classes.
items.documentation:
Thermal-electron collisional power density is the signed local rate of
kinetic-energy transfer from nonthermal particles to the bulk thermal
electron population. It includes all guiding-center orbit classes of the
nonthermal population and represents an energy source or sink, not stored
energy density.

The transfer rate is the kinetic-energy moment of the thermal-electron
collision operator:

$$
P_e^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_a \int \frac{1}{2}m_e |\mathbf{v}|^2 C_{ea}[f_e^{\mathrm{th}},f_a](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_e^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal-electron collisional power density,
$\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $m_e$ is electron mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is
electron velocity, $f_e^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal-electron velocity
distribution, and $f_a$ is the nonthermal velocity distribution of species
$a$. The Coulomb collision operator $C_{ea}$ gives the change in the
thermal-electron distribution caused by collisions with nonthermal species
$a$. The integral covers electron velocity space, and the sum includes all
contributing nonthermal species; multiple nonthermal distributions belonging
to the same species are superposed.

This quantity specializes [electron collisional power
density](name:electron_power_density_due_to_collisions) by selecting bulk
thermal electrons as the target population. It excludes energy gained by
nonthermal electron targets and all noncollisional energy-transfer
mechanisms. No flux-surface averaging or volume integration is implicit; a
flux-surface-averaged member denotes the corresponding average of this local
exchange rate.

The
[co-passing](name:co_passing_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions),
[counter-passing](name:counter_passing_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions),
and [trapped
contributions](name:trapped_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions)
partition the nonthermal donor population, not the thermal-electron target.
These contributions sum to the orbit-unrestricted quantity when evaluated
locally at the same position or subjected to the same spatial average.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer net kinetic
energy to the bulk thermal electron population.

items.name: perpendicular_fast_neutral_pressure
items.description:
Pressure of a suprathermal neutral species is the mean normal kinetic stress
perpendicular to the local magnetic field, averaged over internal states.
items.documentation:
Pressure of a suprathermal neutral species perpendicular to the local
magnetic field is the mean of its two transverse normal kinetic stresses. It
is the field-perpendicular component in a gyrotropic description of neutral
kinetic stress; the magnetic field supplies the reference direction, not a
magnetic confinement force on the neutrals.

The perpendicular pressure is defined by the transverse projection of the
kinetic pressure tensor:

$$
p_{0,\mathrm{fast},\perp} = \left\langle \frac{1}{2}\left(\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{P}_{0,\mathrm{fast},a} - \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf{P}_{0,\mathrm{fast},a}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}\right)\right\rangle_a
$$

where $p_{0,\mathrm{fast},\perp}$ is the perpendicular fast-neutral
pressure, $0$ denotes the neutral population, $a$ labels an internal state,
$\mathbf{P}_{0,\mathrm{fast},a}$ is the kinetic pressure tensor of the
suprathermal neutral species in that state, $\operatorname{tr}$ denotes the
tensor trace, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_a$ denotes averaging over internal
states. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ follows the
local magnetic field $\mathbf B$, which must be nonzero to define this
projection.

The quantity applies to one neutral species and excludes thermal neutrals,
ionized particles, and contributions from other species. When multiple
internal states are present, their perpendicular pressures are averaged
rather than summed; the averaging weights are unspecified. The
[state-resolved perpendicular suprathermal neutral
pressure](name:perpendicular_suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure)
instead applies to one specified internal state.

The transverse projection corresponds to the perpendicular component of
[fast neutral pressure](name:fast_neutral_pressure), but the internal-state
average defined here differs from that parent's internal-state-summed
aggregation. Its directional counterpart is the [parallel fast neutral
pressure](name:parallel_fast_neutral_pressure), which resolves stress along
the local magnetic field rather than across it.

items.name: elongation_of_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Elongation of the plasma boundary is the ratio of its poloidal
cross-section’s vertical extent to its radial extent, independent of overall
size.
items.documentation:
Elongation of plasma boundary

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the defining
relation is:

$$
\kappa = (Z_{\max} - Z_{\min})/(R_{\max} - R_{\min})
$$

where $\kappa$ is the elongation, $Z_{\max}$ and $Z_{\min}$ are the maximum
and minimum vertical coordinates of the plasma-boundary cross-section, and
$R_{\max}$ and $R_{\min}$ are its maximum and minimum major radii.

The extrema apply to the full plasma-boundary cross-section, not an average
over nested surfaces. Equivalently, elongation is the vertical half-height
divided by the geometric minor radius, defined as half the major-radius
width. For an elliptical cross-section with vertically and radially aligned
axes, it equals the vertical-to-horizontal semi-axis ratio; the extent-based
definition does not require an ellipse.

This quantity is the [elongation of a flux
surface](name:elongation_of_flux_surface) evaluated specifically at the
plasma boundary. The [derivative of elongation with respect to normalized
minor
radius](name:derivative_of_elongation_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_normalized_minor_radius)
instead describes how this ratio changes between neighboring surfaces,
rather than the boundary shape ratio itself.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_x_point
items.description:
Signed vertical (Z) coordinate of an X-point, the magnetic null where
separatrix branches meet, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The vertical coordinate of an X-point is its signed height along $Z$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \\phi, Z)$ frame. An X-point is a poloidal
magnetic null at which separatrix branches meet.

This quantity identifies the vertical location of the X-point and is
distinct from the [vertical coordinate of the magnetic
axis](name:vertical_coordinate_of_magnetic_axis) and the [vertical
coordinate of the strike point](name:vertical_coordinate_of_strike_point).

items.name: toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Toroidal deuterium-ion fluid velocity at the core-side shoulder of the
H-mode edge transport barrier, averaged over deuterium ion charge states.
items.documentation:
Deuterium-ion toroidal fluid velocity at the core-side shoulder of the
H-mode edge transport barrier represents the bulk rotational flow of
deuterium ions. It is the density-weighted mean over all deuterium ion
charge states, rather than a thermal speed or velocity magnitude.

$$
v_{phi,D} = \frac{\sum_q n_{D,q} v_{phi,D,q}}{\sum_q n_{D,q}}
$$

where $q$ labels deuterium ion charge state, $n_{D,q}$ is its number density
in m$^{-3}$, and $v_{\phi,D,q}$ is its toroidal fluid-velocity component in
m.s$^{-1}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The locus
is the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, and the
quantity is distinct from the corresponding [toroidal hydrogen-ion
velocity](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top).

items.name: plasma_pressure_real_part
items.description:
Plasma pressure real part is the real quadrature of a complex scalar
representation of isotropic plasma pressure. For perturbation
eigenfunctions, it is the signed real component of the pressure
perturbation, not the full complex eigenfunction.
items.documentation:
Plasma pressure real part is the scalar real quadrature of a complex
representation of isotropic plasma pressure. It represents the component
obtained after the phase convention for the complex pressure quantity has
been fixed, and it is distinct from the complete complex quantity.

The real part is defined by applying the real-part operator to the
corresponding complex plasma-pressure quantity:

$$
p_R = \operatorname{Re}(\tilde{p})
$$

where $p_R$ is the plasma pressure real part, $\tilde{p}$ is the
corresponding complex scalar plasma-pressure quantity, and
$\operatorname{Re}$ denotes extraction of the real component.

This parent quantity is restricted to real-part quantities of isotropic
plasma pressure and does not by itself specify perturbation order,
Fourier-mode labeling, phase normalization, or spatial locus. It applies to
the plasma scalar pressure field; it is not a species-resolved pressure, a
pressure-tensor component, or an anisotropic-pressure component.

It excludes the imaginary quadrature, modulus, phase, and complete complex
pressure quantity. More specific children add the physics qualifier while
preserving the same real-part operation; for example, [perturbed plasma
pressure real part](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure_real_part) is the real
component of a complex first-order plasma-pressure perturbation
eigenfunction. If the corresponding complex quantity is written as
$\tilde{p}=p_R+i p_I$, then $p_I$ is its imaginary quadrature and $i$ is the
imaginary unit, while this name denotes only $p_R$.

Sign convention: Positive when the selected real quadrature denotes an
increase of isotropic plasma pressure relative to the reference pressure
state.

items.name: parallel_fluctuating_ion_current_density
items.description:
Temporal standard deviation of the total ion charge-current density after
projection onto the local magnetic-field direction at a plasma-facing probe.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the temporal standard deviation of the total ion-carried
charge-current density after projection onto the local magnetic-field
direction at the specified plasma-facing probe. Ion contributions from all
included species and charge states are summed with their signed charge
weighting before the fluctuation statistic is evaluated. It is the parallel
specialization of [fluctuating ion current
density](name:fluctuating_ion_current_density).

With $t$ denoting time in seconds, the defining relation is:

$$
\sigma_{j_i,\parallel}=\left\langle\left[j_{i,\parallel}(t)-\left\langle j_{i,\parallel}\right\rangle_t\right]^2\right\rangle_t^{1/2},\qquad j_{i,\parallel}(t)=\mathbf{j}_i(t)\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}(t),\qquad \hat{\mathbf b}(t)=\frac{\mathbf{B}(t)}{|\mathbf{B}(t)|}
$$

Here $\mathbf{j}_i$ is the aggregated ion current-density vector in A
m$^{-2}$, $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic
field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field in tesla, and
$\langle\cdot\rangle_t$ denotes the temporal average.

The aggregation and projection precede the standard-deviation operation;
this is not a sum of separately calculated species fluctuations. Unlike
[fluctuating saturated ion current
density](name:fluctuating_saturated_ion_current_density), it represents the
total ion current rather than only the ion-saturation current component. The
result is nonnegative even when the underlying parallel current changes
sign.

items.name: deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Number density of the effective deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species at
the divertor target is the local particle count per volume at the
plasma-side sheath entrance.
items.documentation:
Number density of the deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species at the
divertor target is the local particle count per volume at the sheath
entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is
the deuterium-tritium-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local deuterium-tritium number density is defined by the differential
particle count:

$$
n_{DT} = \frac{dN_{DT}}{dV}
$$

where $N_{DT}$ is the number of particles represented by the effective
deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species, and $V$ is a small plasma volume
whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the
divertor target.

This quantity applies to the ion population represented as one effective
deuterium-tritium fuel species, rather than to separately resolved deuterium
and tritium populations. It includes the positive ionic states represented
by that pseudo-species and excludes neutral deuterium-tritium atoms or
molecules, electrons, and other ion species.

The localized quantity is the divertor-target counterpart of
[deuterium_tritium_density](name:deuterium_tritium_density). Unlike
[deuterium_density_at_divertor_target](name:deuterium_density_at_divertor_target)
and
[tritium_density_at_divertor_target](name:tritium_density_at_divertor_target),
which describe the separately resolved isotope populations, this quantity
uses the prescribed effective deuterium-tritium pseudo-species.

items.name: diameter_of_diagnostic_aperture
items.description:
Full transverse diameter of a circular diagnostic aperture, measured across
its center between opposite points on the circumferential boundary.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the full transverse extent of the clear circular opening at
the diagnostic entrance pupil, measured between opposite points on its
circumferential boundary.

The diameter is defined by

$$
D = 2r
$$

where $D$ is the aperture diameter and $r$ is the geometric radius given by
the [radius of the diagnostic aperture](name:radius_of_diagnostic_aperture).

The quantity describes the opening geometry only; it excludes aperture
