thickness, housing dimensions, and the width of a noncircular aperture. The
diameter determines the geometric area and contributes to the solid-angle
acceptance together with the aperture-to-source distance.

items.name: alfven_time
items.description:
Characteristic shear-Alfvén transit time across the magnetic-axis
major-radius scale, set by local ion inertia and the reference
magnetic-field strength.
items.documentation:
The Alfvén time is the characteristic shear-Alfvén propagation time across a
reference major-radius scale in the confined plasma. It is a physical MHD
timescale, not an event timestamp or a growth rate.

Its defining relation is

$$
\tau_A(\rho) = \frac{R_0\sqrt{m_i n_i(\rho)}}{B_0}
$$

where $\tau_A(\rho)$ is the local Alfvén time, $R_0$ is the magnetic-axis
major-radius scale, $m_i$ is the mass of the reference ion population,
$n_i(\rho)$ is its number density at radial coordinate $\rho$, and $B_0$ is
the reference magnetic-field strength.

The quantity applies locally at each radial coordinate in the confined
plasma; it is not a radial average or radial integral, and it does not
represent a charge-state-resolved time unless the reference ion population
is so specified. As a timescale, it is distinct from the frequency
represented by [alfven_frequency](name:alfven_frequency) and from the
general temporal quantity time. It provides the characteristic time used to
normalize MHD growth rates and other dynamical rates.

items.name: total_hydrogenic_density
items.description:
Hydrogen-isotope abundance measure derived from included charge states and
isotopes, either averaged along a line or over a volume or used to normalize
neutral-state density.
items.documentation:
Hydrogenic-density-derived quantities quantify the abundance of
hydrogen-isotope particles with the included isotopic species and charge
states. Depending on the derivative, the total density is averaged along a
line, averaged over a volume, or used as the reference denominator for a
neutral-state composition fraction.

The underlying [hydrogenic density](name:hydrogenic_density) is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{H}} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{H}} \sum_q n_{s,q}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the total hydrogenic number density, $\mathcal{H}$
is the set of included hydrogen-isotope species, $q$ is charge state, and
$n_{s,q}$ is the number density of species $s$ in state $q$.

The line-averaged total hydrogenic density and volume-averaged total
hydrogenic density retain density character under their respective averaging
operations. The [neutral-state density
ratio](name:ratio_of_neutral_state_density_to_total_hydrogenic_density) is
instead a composition fraction formed by dividing a neutral charge-state
density by $n_{\mathrm{H}}$, and is therefore not itself a density.

items.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional power transferred to the thermal
(Maxwellian) ion population of a specified species and charge state.
items.documentation:
Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional power transferred to the thermal
(Maxwellian) ion population of a specified species and charge state,
obtained by integrating the local Coulomb-collisional energy-exchange rate
density over the plasma volume.

It is defined as the volume integral of the local collisional
energy-exchange rate density for that thermal charge-state population:

$$
P_{\rm th}^{s,z} = \int_{V_{\rm p}} q_{\rm th,coll}^{s,z}(\mathbf{x}) \, dV
$$

where $P_{\rm th}^{s,z}$ is the thermal ion charge-state collisional power,
$q_{\rm th,coll}^{s,z}$ is the local Coulomb-collisional energy-exchange
rate density for thermal ions of species $s$ and charge state $z$, $V_{\rm
p}$ is the plasma volume, and $\mathbf{x}$ denotes position.

Together with the [fast ion charge state power due to
collisions](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions), it forms
the [total ion charge state power due to
collisions](name:total_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions) for the
same species and charge state through $P_{\rm coll}^{s,z}=P_{\rm
th}^{s,z}+P_{\rm fast}^{s,z}$. The aggregate [thermal ion power due to
collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions) is recovered only
after summing over all thermal ion species and charge states, $P_{\rm
th}=\sum_s\sum_z P_{\rm th}^{s,z}$; summing only over charge states of one
species gives a species-resolved contribution rather than the all-species
thermal aggregate.

Sign convention: Positive when the specified thermal ion charge state is a
net recipient of energy from Coulomb collisions.

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_nitrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description:
Dimensionless abundance ratio of charge-state-summed nitrogen nuclei to
electrons, with both number densities averaged over the plasma volume
bounded by the last closed flux surface.
items.documentation:
Dimensionless abundance ratio of charge-state-summed nitrogen nuclei to
electrons, with both number densities averaged over the plasma volume
bounded by the last closed flux surface. It represents the species-level
nitrogen abundance relative to the free-electron population in the confined
plasma.

The defining ratio is:

$$
f_{\mathrm{N/e}} = \frac{\left\langle \sum_{q=0}^{7} n_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}} \right\rangle_V}{\left\langle n_e \right\rangle_V}
$$

where $f_{\mathrm{N/e}}$ is the nitrogen-to-electron abundance ratio,
$n_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}}$ is the nitrogen number density in charge state $q$,
$q=0$ denotes neutral nitrogen, $q=7$ denotes fully stripped nitrogen, $n_e$
is the [electron density](name:electron_density), and
$\langle\cdot\rangle_V$ denotes averaging over the plasma volume bounded by
the last closed flux surface.

The numerator is the charge-state-summed [nitrogen
density](name:nitrogen_density) after volume averaging, equivalently the
[volume-averaged nitrogen density](name:volume_averaged_nitrogen_density).
The denominator is the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density) evaluated with the same
volume-averaging convention.

This quantity is a ratio of separate volume averages, not the volume average
of a local nitrogen-to-electron density ratio. It is species-level and
charge-state-summed, so it differs from any charge-state-resolved nitrogen
abundance that retains a single ionization state in the numerator. It
follows the same abundance-ratio convention as [ratio of volume-averaged
neon density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_neon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density)
and [ratio of volume-averaged iron density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_iron_density_to_electron_density).

items.name: momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential
items.description:
Momentum flux due to a perturbed parallel vector potential is the
dimensionless signed contribution to plasma momentum transport produced by
turbulent fluctuations of the electromagnetic vector potential component
parallel to the magnetic field. It is expressed relative to a positive
reference momentum-flux scale.
items.documentation:
Momentum flux due to a perturbed parallel vector potential is the
contribution to plasma momentum transport produced by turbulent fluctuations
of the electromagnetic vector potential component parallel to the magnetic
field. It is a signed scalar contribution expressed relative to a positive
reference momentum-flux scale, so its sign is inherited from the underlying
momentum transport rather than from the scale.

The scaled contribution is defined by

$$
\widehat{\Pi}_{A_\parallel} = \frac{\Pi_{A_\parallel}}{\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $\widehat{\Pi}_{A_\parallel}$ denotes this quantity,
$\Pi_{A_\parallel}$ is the physical momentum-flux contribution due to
perturbed parallel-vector-potential fluctuations, $A_\parallel$ is the
component of the electromagnetic vector potential parallel to the magnetic
field, and $\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference momentum-flux
scale.

This parent fixes the fluctuation mechanism to the perturbed $A_\parallel$
contribution. The parent-level scaling requires only a positive reference
momentum-flux scale; it does not select a named normalization convention, a
toroidal or other momentum component, a species population, a flux-surface
or geometric projection, an averaging domain, or a velocity-space channel.
It denotes the mechanism-selected scalar aggregate over distinctions not
explicitly resolved by a specialization, not a channel-resolved or
component-resolved flux.

This quantity is distinct from local momentum density, from the total
momentum flux formed by summing all fluctuation mechanisms, and from
momentum-flux contributions driven by other turbulent fields. A concrete
child such as [normalized momentum flux due to a perturbed parallel vector
potential](name:momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential)
retains the same perturbed-$A_\parallel$ mechanism while fixing a particular
normalized turbulence quantity and additional component or channel scope; it
is not a statement that the parent lacks the $A_\parallel$ mechanism or
receives a second normalization.

Sign convention: Positive when, for the momentum component and
transport-surface orientation in scope, this contribution carries positive
momentum through the surface in the positive-normal direction.

items.name: net_thermal_power_of_breeder_blanket_module
items.description:
Net thermal power transferred from a single breeder blanket module to its
coolant, summed over all coolant branches as an enthalpy increase.
items.documentation:
Coolant thermal power of a single breeder blanket module is the net rate at
which heat leaves the module through its coolant circuits. It aggregates the
thermal energy carried by every coolant branch serving that module,
regardless of whether the heat originated from nuclear deposition or
absorbed incident radiation.

The defining branch balance is

$$
P_{\mathrm{cool}} = \sum_b \dot{m}_b\left(h_{b,\mathrm{out}} - h_{b,\mathrm{in}}\right)
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{cool}}$ is the coolant-transferred power, $b$ indexes
coolant branches, $\dot{m}_b$ is the mass flow rate in branch $b$, and
$h_{b,\mathrm{in}}$ and $h_{b,\mathrm{out}}$ are its inlet and outlet
specific enthalpies. The quantity is the coolant-transferred component of
thermal power of a breeder blanket module, distinct from source-specific
quantities such as [nuclear heating power of a breeder blanket
module](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_module) and [absorbed
radiated power of a breeder blanket
module](name:absorbed_radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module).

items.name: accumulated_oxygen_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Cumulative oxygen gas introduced during the prefill phase by gas injection,
expressed as an equivalent-electron count where each oxygen atom contributes
8 count units equal to its atomic number.
items.documentation:
The prefill phase precedes plasma breakdown, during which controlled gas
injection establishes an initial neutral gas background in the vessel. This
quantity accumulates the total oxygen inventory delivered during that phase,
representing each oxygen atom as 8 equivalent electrons equal to the atomic
number $Z_\mathrm{O} = 8$.

The equivalent-electron inventory is defined as:

$$
N_\mathrm{eq} = Z_\mathrm{O} \cdot N_\mathrm{O}
$$

where $N_\mathrm{O}$ is the total number of oxygen atoms injected during the
prefill interval and $Z_\mathrm{O} = 8$ is the atomic number of oxygen.

The count is inferred from calibrated gas injection valve records integrated
over the prefill interval, from the start of the prefill phase through
plasma breakdown. It is the accumulated component of
oxygen_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection and follows the same
equivalent-electron convention applied to helium-3 in
[accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection)
and to lithium in
[accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection).
Post-breakdown oxygen injection is tracked separately by
[oxygen_count](name:oxygen_count_accumulated_due_to_gas_injection).

items.name: ion_average_temperature
items.description:
Temperature of the combined ion population, given by the
number-density-weighted mean over all ion species and states, including all
ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Temperature of the combined ion population is the number-density-weighted
mean of the temperatures of all ion species and ion states. It characterizes
random ion kinetic energy rather than directed-flow energy.

The population average is defined by

$$
T_i = \frac{\sum_s\sum_a n_{s,a}T_{s,a}}{\sum_s\sum_a n_{s,a}}
$$

where $T_i$ is the combined ion temperature, $s$ labels ion species, $a$
labels the states of each species, $n_{s,a}$ is the number density of that
species and state, and $T_{s,a}$ is its temperature. The sums include all
ion species and all ion states, including all ionic charge states; the total
ion number density in the denominator must be nonzero.

The averaging combines ion populations at the same spatial evaluation
location, not temperatures across a spatial region. It is a density-weighted
mean, not a sum of temperatures or an equal-weight mean over species.
Electrons and neutral particles are excluded; unlike [plasma
temperature](name:plasma_temperature), it does not combine ion and electron
thermal contributions.

When the included population consists of thermal ions, this mean corresponds
to the [total ion temperature](name:total_ion_temperature), which likewise
combines species and charge-state contributions through number-density
weighting.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_plasma_filament
items.description:
Radial coordinate of a plasma filament is the major-radius coordinate, in
the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of the oblique reference point
anchoring one current-carrying filament element's rectangular cross-section.
items.documentation:
Radial coordinate of a plasma filament is the major-radius coordinate of the
oblique reference point that anchors one current-carrying plasma filament
element's rectangular cross-section. It is defined in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius from the machine
symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies to a single plasma filament element represented by
oblique rectangular cross-sectional geometry. It is the coordinate of the
reference point used by that representation, not the filament width, height,
centroid position, magnetic-axis position, or a flux-surface radial
coordinate; no averaging or summation over filament elements is implied.

Together with the vertical coordinate of the plasma filament, it locates the
oblique reference point in the poloidal plane. The [alpha angle of the
plasma filament](name:alpha_angle_of_plasma_filament) and beta angle of the
plasma filament are defined relative to this same reference point, and the
[plasma filament width](name:plasma_filament_width) is a rectangular
cross-section extent anchored by it.

items.name: volume_averaged_iron_density
items.description:
Volume-averaged iron density is the total number density of iron ions,
summed over Fe1+ through Fe26+ and averaged over the confined plasma volume.
items.documentation:
Volume-averaged iron density is the total number density of iron ions,
aggregated over all iron charge states from Fe$^{1+}$ through Fe$^{26+}$ and
averaged throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the spatially averaged
form of [iron_density](name:iron_density), not a charge-state-resolved
quantity.

The volume-averaged density is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{p}}} \int_{V_{\mathrm{p}}} \left(\sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}(\mathbf{r})\right)\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the volume-averaged iron density in
m$^{-3}$, $V_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the confined plasma volume in m$^{3}$,
$n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local density of iron charge state
$z$, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $dV$ is a volume element.

Neutral iron is excluded, and the result does not preserve the distribution
among charge states. It differs from
[volume_averaged_ion_density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density) through its
fixed iron-species scope and from
[iron_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:iron_density_at_magnetic_axis) because
it represents a volume average rather than a local axis value.

items.name: x_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
items.description:
X-axis component of the unit vector defining an electron-cyclotron launcher
mirror’s translation or rotation axis at its home position.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the Cartesian x projection of the unit vector that defines
an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror’s translation direction or rotation
axis at its home position.

Let $\hat{d}$ denote this direction unit vector and $\hat{x}$ the x-axis
unit vector in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$
basis. The component is defined by

$$
d_x = \hat{d} \cdot \hat{x}
$$

where $d_x$ is the signed x-axis component and the unit-vector condition is
$|\hat{d}|=1$.

The component is dimensionless and is bounded by $-1 \leq d_x \leq 1$.
Together with the [y-axis direction
component](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror)
and [z-axis direction
component](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror),
it specifies the mirror-axis orientation.

items.name: inner_radius_of_antenna_strap
items.description:
Inner radius of an antenna strap is the perpendicular distance from the
strap conductor axis to the inner cylindrical boundary of its annular
cross-section.
items.documentation:
Inner radius of an antenna strap is the perpendicular distance from the
strap conductor axis to the inner cylindrical boundary of its annular
cross-section. It identifies the inner boundary of the conductor material
and is the smaller of the two annular boundary radii.

Use [radius of antenna strap](name:radius_of_antenna_strap) for the
boundary-radius concept without selecting a surface, and [outer radius of
antenna strap](name:outer_radius_of_antenna_strap) for the larger boundary
radius. If $r_\mathrm{in}$ and $r_\mathrm{out}$ denote the inner and outer
radii, respectively, then $0 \le r_\mathrm{in} \le r_\mathrm{out}$. This
quantity is distinct from the [height of antenna
strap](name:height_of_antenna_strap), [toroidal width of antenna
strap](name:toroidal_width_of_antenna_strap), and [thickness of antenna
strap](name:thickness_of_antenna_strap).

items.name: current_of_rogowski_coil
items.description:
Signed conventional current threading a Rogowski-coil winding contour, with
orientation set by the coil's assigned normal.
items.documentation:
Signed conventional current threading a Rogowski-coil winding contour is the
net conventional electric current crossing an oriented surface bounded by
that contour. The surface orientation is specified by the coil's assigned
normal and the associated right-hand rule for the contour.

The enclosed current is defined by the surface integral of conventional
current density:

$$
I_{\mathrm{enc}} = \int_S \mathbf{J} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dS
$$

where $S$ is any surface whose boundary is the Rogowski-coil contour,
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the assigned unit normal to that surface, and
$\mathbf{J}$ is the conventional electric current density.

This is an enclosed-current quantity, not the electrical current carried by
the Rogowski-coil sensor winding. In the Rogowski-coil principle, the
induced winding voltage is proportional to $dI_{\mathrm{enc}}/dt$;
$I_{\mathrm{enc}}$ is the current whose time variation drives that signal.

Sign convention: Positive when the net conventional current crosses the
oriented surface in the direction of the assigned normal.

items.name: toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal flow velocity of carbon impurity ions at the
core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, resolved along
increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The carbon impurity-ion fluid velocity at the H-mode pedestal top is the
density-weighted bulk-flow velocity of all contributing carbon ion charge
states, evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport
barrier. It is the toroidal component rather than the total
three-dimensional speed, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

$$
v_{\phi,C}=\frac{\sum_q n_{C^{q+}}v_{\phi,C^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{C^{q+}}}
$$

Here, $q$ indexes the contributing carbon ion charge states, $n_{C^{q+}}$ is
the corresponding number density in m$^{-3}$, and $v_{\phi,C^{q+}}$ is its
toroidal velocity in m s$^{-1}$. Neutral carbon is excluded because this
quantity is defined for impurity ions. The pedestal-top value is distinct
from the [toroidal carbon velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

Sign convention: Positive when the carbon-ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: nitrogen_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Nitrogen ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a
plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all ionization states and
excluding neutral nitrogen.
items.documentation:
Nitrogen density at a limiter is the local number density of nitrogen ions
in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter
surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic
presheath or sheath entrance, where the limiter terminates open field lines
in the scrape-off layer.

The charge-state-summed density is defined from the velocity distribution
functions by:

$$
n_{\mathrm{N}} = \sum_{q=1}^{q_{\max}} \int f_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $q$ is the positive nitrogen ion charge state, $q_{\max}$ is the
highest included ionization state, and $f_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}}(\mathbf{v})$ is
the velocity distribution function of that ion state at the evaluation
point.

This is the nitrogen-specific component of
[density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter). It excludes neutral nitrogen
and is distinct from
[neon_density_at_limiter](name:neon_density_at_limiter), which applies the
same boundary definition to neon ions.

items.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Toroidal component of the momentum-convection velocity for ions of one
specified species and charge state, evaluated at the maximum-major-radius
point of each magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the velocity associated with
momentum convection for ions of one selected species and charge state. It is
a velocity component, not an angular rotation frequency.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the component
is the projection

$$
v_{s,q,\phi} = \mathbf{v}_{s,q} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_{s,q,\phi}$ is this quantity, $\mathbf{v}_{s,q}$ is the
momentum-convection velocity vector for ion species $s$ and charge state
$q$, $s$ identifies the ion species, $q$ identifies its charge state, and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal
angle.

The quantity is resolved for one ion species and one charge state and is
evaluated at the point of maximum major radius on each magnetic flux
surface, not as a surface average. It is not summed over charge states; the
species-level [toroidal ion momentum convection
velocity](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_convection_velocity) is the
density-weighted mean over all charge states. This scalar is the toroidal
component of the [ion charge-state momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) vector and is
distinct from its [radial
component](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity), which
is along $\hat{R}$. It is a linear velocity component, distinct from the
[toroidal ion charge-state rotation
frequency](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency), an angular
rate.

Sign convention: Positive when the velocity component points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: ion_charge_state_particle_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective velocity multiplying the density of a specified ion charge state
in its convective cross-field particle transport.
items.documentation:
The ion-charge-state particle convection velocity is the effective
coefficient of the density-proportional, convective contribution to
transport of a specified ion charge state across magnetic flux surfaces. It
is the ion-charge-state specialization of particle convection velocity, not
a velocity magnitude.

The convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_s^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_s v_s^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\Gamma_s^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective particle flux of the
specified ion charge state, $n_s$ is its particle number density, and
$v_s^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this convection velocity.

This quantity excludes density-gradient-driven diffusive transport and is
not summed over other ion charge states. The magnitude-only counterpart
[ion-state particle convection velocity
magnitude](name:ion_state_particle_convection_velocity_magnitude) removes
the directional sign.

Sign convention: Positive when the convective particle flux of the specified
ion charge state follows the positive orientation assigned to the underlying
transport coordinate.

items.name: ratio_of_neutral_state_density_to_total_hydrogenic_density
items.description:
Abundance fraction of hydrogenic particles in a specified neutral internal
state, defined as the neutral internal-state density divided by the total
hydrogenic density. It is bounded from 0 to 1 when that state population is
included in the denominator.
items.documentation:
Abundance fraction of hydrogenic particles in a specified neutral internal
state is the number-density ratio between that state and the complete
hydrogenic population. It represents the occupation of the specified neutral
internal state within the hydrogenic ensemble.

The fraction is defined by

$$
f_{n,s} = \frac{n_{n,s}}{n_{H,\mathrm{tot}}}
$$

where $n_{n,s}$ is the [neutral internal-state
density](name:neutral_internal_state_density) for state $s$ and
$n_{H,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the [total hydrogenic
density](name:total_hydrogenic_density).

The denominator is the total hydrogenic population, not only the neutral
population or only the same internal-state manifold. For a state population
that is part of the total hydrogenic population, $0 \le f_{n,s} \le 1$. This
quantity differs from the [cold neutral
fraction](name:cold_neutral_fraction), which partitions the hydrogenic
population by cold-neutral component rather than by occupation of a single
neutral internal state.

items.name: current_of_divertor_tile
items.description:
Conventional electric current of a divertor tile is the net signed charge
current crossing the electrostatic sheath from the plasma onto the
plasma-facing surface of one individual divertor tile.
items.documentation:
Conventional electric current of a divertor tile is the net signed charge
current crossing the electrostatic sheath from the plasma onto the
plasma-facing surface of one individual divertor tile. It is a tile-level
incident sheath current, expressed using the direction of conventional
electric current rather than electron particle flow.

The current is the sheath-normal surface integral of the conventional
electric current density over the tile surface:

$$
I_\mathrm{tile} = \int_{S_\mathrm{tile}} \mathbf{j} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{p}\to\mathrm{tile}} \, dS
$$

where $I_\mathrm{tile}$ is the conventional electric current of the divertor
tile, $S_\mathrm{tile}$ is the plasma-facing surface of that tile,
$\mathbf{j}$ is the conventional electric current density,
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{p}\to\mathrm{tile}}$ is the surface normal
directed from the plasma toward the tile, and $dS$ is the surface-area
element.

The scope is one individual divertor tile and the aggregation is the net
charge-weighted contribution of all charged species crossing the sheath onto
that tile surface. It is not the current of a complete divertor target, not
the current of an entire divertor, and not an electrical-conduction current
in supports or external circuitry after charge has entered the solid.

The [current at a divertor target](name:current_at_divertor_target) is
obtained by summing this quantity over the divertor tiles that constitute
that target. The [current of a divertor](name:current_of_divertor) is
obtained by summing the corresponding tile or target contributions over the
divertor.

Sign convention: Positive when conventional electric current crosses the
electrostatic sheath from the plasma toward the plasma-facing surface of the
divertor tile.

items.name: y_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector
items.description:
Y direction unit-vector component of a neutron detector is the y direction
cosine, in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) basis, of the unit vector
from a field-of-view voxel center toward the detector center.
items.documentation:
Y direction unit-vector component of a neutron detector is the signed
projection, in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$
basis, of the unit vector directed from a field-of-view voxel center toward
the detector center. It is the y direction cosine of that line-of-sight
direction.

The component is defined by projecting the detector-directed unit vector
onto the $\hat{y}$ basis vector:

$$
u_y = \hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{det}} \cdot \hat{y} = \frac{(\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{det}} - \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{vox}}) \cdot \hat{y}}{\lVert \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{det}} - \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{vox}} \rVert}
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the unit vector from the
field-of-view voxel center to the detector center,
$\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the detector-center position,
$\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{vox}}$ is the field-of-view voxel-center position, and
$\hat{y}$ is the y basis vector of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},
\hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame.

This quantity is a signed direction-cosine component, not a position
coordinate, distance, or unnormalized displacement component. Together with
the corresponding x and z components it satisfies $u_x^2 + u_y^2 + u_z^2 =
1$ when the field-of-view voxel center and detector center are distinct.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection
items.description:
Neutral internal-state velocity due to convection is a scalar
advective-velocity quantity characterizing convective transport of neutral
particles in a specified internal quantum state. It does not by itself
choose a spatial projection or effective-vector convention; concrete
specializations provide that extra semantics.
items.documentation:
Neutral internal-state velocity due to convection is a scalar
advective-velocity quantity characterizing convective transport of neutral
particles in a specified internal quantum state. It denotes the velocity
factor for the convective part of state-resolved neutral-particle transport,
abstracted over the particular scalar component, projection, magnitude, or
effective reduction chosen by a concrete specialization.

For any scalar realization $q$ of the convective neutral flux for internal
state $a$, the defining relation is

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{conv},a}^{(q)} = n_a v_{\mathrm{conv},a}^{(q)}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{conv},a}^{(q)}$ is the scalar convective
particle-flux realization for neutrals in internal state $a$, $n_a$ is the
neutral-particle number density in that internal state, and
$v_{\mathrm{conv},a}^{(q)}$ is the corresponding neutral internal-state
velocity due to convection.

This parent name is not the unprojected vector itself and does not define a
unique positive direction. A child such as [effective neutral internal-state
velocity due to
convection](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection)
specializes the parent by adding the effective, unprojected-vector
interpretation; other children may specialize it by component, projection,
or magnitude semantics.

items.name: toroidal_magnetic_field_at_ferritic_element_centroid
items.description:
Signed projection of the magnetic-field vector onto the toroidal direction
at a ferritic element’s geometric centroid.
items.documentation:
The toroidal magnetic-field component at a ferritic element’s geometric
centroid is the projection of the local magnetic-field vector onto the
toroidal direction. The projection is defined in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

$$
B_\phi(\mathbf r_c) = \mathbf B(\mathbf r_c) \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf B$ is the magnetic-field vector, $\mathbf r_c$ is the
ferritic-element centroid position, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle.

This quantity is the toroidal counterpart of the [radial magnetic field at a
ferritic element
centroid](name:radial_magnetic_field_at_ferritic_element_centroid) and
[vertical magnetic field at a ferritic element
centroid](name:vertical_magnetic_field_at_ferritic_element_centroid). It
describes magnetic field, not the material magnetization represented by
[toroidal magnetization of a ferritic
element](name:toroidal_magnetization_of_ferritic_element).

Sign convention: Positive when $B_\phi$ points in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: electron_velocity
items.description:
Local bulk-flow velocity of the electron fluid, defined by the
density-weighted first moment of its velocity distribution and distinct from
random thermal motion.
items.documentation:
Electron fluid velocity is the local bulk translational velocity of the
electron population, describing collective advective motion rather than the
random thermal motion of individual electrons.

At position $\mathbf{x}$, the velocity is defined by the first moment of the
electron distribution:

$$
\mathbf{u}_e(\mathbf{x})=\frac{1}{n_e(\mathbf{x})}\int \mathbf{v}\,f_e(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v,\qquad n_e(\mathbf{x})=\int f_e(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_e$ is the electron fluid velocity in m s$^{-1}$,
$\mathbf{x}$ is position in m, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity in m
s$^{-1}$, $f_e$ is the electron velocity distribution, and $n_e$ is electron
number density in m$^{-3}$.

This is the complete vector before directional projection. Its projections
include [radial electron velocity](name:radial_electron_velocity), [toroidal
electron velocity](name:toroidal_electron_velocity), [vertical electron
velocity](name:vertical_electron_velocity), [poloidal electron
velocity](name:poloidal_electron_velocity), and [parallel electron
velocity](name:parallel_electron_velocity). It is distinct from the bulk
velocities of ions and neutrals, such as [ion velocity](name:ion_velocity)
and [neutral velocity](name:neutral_velocity).

items.name: vertical_vorticity
items.description:
Projection of the curl of plasma center-of-mass velocity along the toroidal
symmetry axis, measuring signed local rotation of the bulk flow.
items.documentation:
Vertical vorticity is the component of plasma [vorticity](name:vorticity)
parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis. For solid-body rotation, it is twice
the vertical component of a fluid element's angular velocity.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the vertical
projection of the velocity curl is

$$
\omega_Z = (\nabla \times \mathbf{v}) \cdot \hat{Z} = \frac{1}{R}\left(\frac{\partial(Rv_\phi)}{\partial R} - \frac{\partial v_R}{\partial \phi}\right)
$$

where $\omega_Z$ is vertical vorticity, $\mathbf{v}$ is the plasma
[center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity), and $\nabla\times$
is the right-handed curl operator. Here $R$ is major radius measured from
the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical
height, and $\hat{Z}$ is the unit vector along increasing height. The
quantities $v_R$ and $v_\phi$ are the cylindrical radial and toroidal
components of $\mathbf{v}$, respectively.

The quantity describes the local mass-weighted plasma bulk flow rather than
a separately selected species or charge state. It carries no surface,
volume, or time averaging and does not assume axisymmetry. It is a signed
component, not vorticity magnitude, vertical velocity, strain rate, or flow
divergence.

Unlike [parallel vorticity](name:parallel_vorticity), which projects the
same curl along the local magnetic field, vertical vorticity uses the fixed
symmetry-axis direction. Dividing this component by the local major radius
gives the distinct [ratio of vertical vorticity to major
radius](name:ratio_of_vertical_vorticity_to_major_radius); that
inverse-radius scaling is not included here.

Sign convention: Positive when the local rotational part of the bulk flow
follows the right-hand rule about $+\hat{Z}$.

items.name: volume_averaged_deuterium_density
items.description:
Deuterium ion density averaged over the plasma volume is the mean local
number density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population.
items.documentation:
Deuterium ion density averaged over the plasma volume is the mean local
number density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population. It is the
charge-state-summed spatial average of the local [deuterium
density](name:deuterium_density).

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_D = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_D(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_D$ is the volume-averaged deuterium density, $V$ is the
specified plasma-volume domain, and $n_D(\mathbf{r})$ is the local deuterium
density at position $\mathbf{r}$. The local density is summed over positive
ionization states and excludes neutral atoms, molecular deuterium, and
non-deuterium species.

This quantity averages over the specified plasma volume rather than along a
chord; the latter is represented by [line-averaged deuterium
density](name:line_averaged_deuterium_density).

items.name: binormal_wave_magnetic_field
items.description:
Signed component of the oscillatory electromagnetic-wave magnetic
perturbation along the local binormal direction, distinct from the total
binormal magnetic field.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the binormal component of the oscillatory magnetic
perturbation carried by a coherent electromagnetic wave. It excludes
equilibrium and other static magnetic-field contributions.

For a harmonic-wave phasor representation, the component amplitude is
defined by projection on the local binormal unit vector:

$$
\widetilde{B}_{\mathrm{wave,bi}}(\mathbf{r},\omega)=\widetilde{\mathbf{B}}_{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r},\omega)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{bi}}(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $\omega$ is angular frequency,
$\widetilde{\mathbf{B}}_{\mathrm{wave}}$ is the complex amplitude of the
wave magnetic field, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{bi}}$ is the local binormal
unit vector, and $\widetilde{B}_{\mathrm{wave,bi}}$ is the complex amplitude
of the binormal component. The corresponding physical time-dependent
component is obtained from the real part of the phasor convention; real- and
imaginary-part quantities are phase-resolved representations, not alternate
definitions of this field.

The binormal direction is tangent to a magnetic flux surface and
perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic-field direction, distinguishing
this quantity from the [parallel wave magnetic
field](name:parallel_wave_magnetic_field). It is the magnetic-field analog
of the [binormal wave electric field](name:binormal_wave_electric_field).

Sign convention: Positive when the wave magnetic-field projection is along
the declared positive binormal unit vector.

items.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity_imaginary_part
items.description:
Imaginary part of the complex amplitude of the radial plasma-velocity
perturbation for toroidal harmonic index n in linear MHD stability analysis.
Radial denotes the component along the R direction in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Imaginary part of the complex amplitude of the radial plasma-velocity
perturbation is the quadrature component of the cylindrical $R$ projection
of the first-order plasma velocity eigenfunction for a specified toroidal
harmonic index $n$. The radial projection is along $\hat{R}$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with basis
$(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The complex radial perturbation amplitude and its contribution to the
single-mode physical perturbation are represented by

$$
\delta v_R^{\mathrm{phys},(n)}(\mathbf{x},t)
=
\operatorname{Re}\!\left[
\left(\delta v_{R,\mathrm{re}}^{(n)}(\mathbf{x})
+i\,\delta v_{R,\mathrm{im}}^{(n)}(\mathbf{x})\right)
e^{i(n\phi-\omega t)}
\right]
$$

where $\delta v_{R,\mathrm{im}}^{(n)}$ is this quantity, $\delta
v_{R,\mathrm{re}}^{(n)}$ is
[radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part),
$\delta v_R^{\mathrm{phys},(n)}$ is the corresponding real physical
perturbation component, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\phi$ is the toroidal
angle of that position, $t$ is time, $\omega$ is the complex mode angular
frequency under the chosen temporal phase convention, $n$ is the integer
toroidal harmonic index, and $i$ is the imaginary unit.

The real and imaginary parts together reconstruct the complex radial
amplitude
[radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity). A
change of the arbitrary global eigenmode phase rotates these two parts, so
this imaginary part is meaningful only with the same phase reference and
eigenfunction normalization as the other perturbation components. It is the
cylindrical $R$ component, not a flux-surface-normal component and not a
component perpendicular to the magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when $\delta v_{R,\mathrm{im}}^{(n)}$ points in
the $+\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: toroidal_mhd_mode_number
items.description:
Dimensionless integer Fourier index specifying toroidal periodicity of a
magnetohydrodynamic perturbation, including the perturbation harmonic
associated with a particle-orbit integral.
items.documentation:
Toroidal MHD mode number is a dimensionless integer Fourier index that
specifies periodic structure around the symmetry axis for a
magnetohydrodynamic perturbation. It identifies a toroidal angular harmonic
rather than a radial branch, harmonic amplitude, or spatial wavevector.

The toroidal harmonic dependence is defined by

$$
\delta F(\phi) = \widetilde{F}\exp(i n_\phi\phi)
$$

where $\delta F$ is a complex harmonic of a perturbed physical quantity,
$\widetilde{F}$ is its complex amplitude independent of toroidal angle, $i$
is the imaginary unit, and $n_\phi$ is the toroidal MHD mode number. The
toroidal angle $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed from above in
the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from
the symmetry axis and $Z$ is vertical height. Other coordinates and time are
held fixed in this expression.

Each value labels one harmonic, not a sum or average over modes. The
absolute value $|n_\phi|$ counts toroidal phase cycles per complete circuit;
$n_\phi=0$ denotes an axisymmetric perturbation. This definition applies to
linear MHD eigenmodes and tearing-mode perturbations. For an associated
particle [orbit integral](name:orbit_integral), it identifies the
perturbation harmonic considered, not an ordinal position in a list of modes
or the value of the integral.

This index is the toroidal component of the [MHD mode-number
vector](name:mhd_mode_number). Together with the [poloidal mode
number](name:poloidal_mode_number), it specifies the angular harmonic
structure and helicity of the perturbation.

items.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode_center
items.description:
Dimensionless magnetic-surface label locating the resonant flux surface at
the center of a neoclassical tearing-mode magnetic island.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the normalized toroidal-flux label of the magnetic surface
passing through the center of a neoclassical tearing-mode magnetic island.
It identifies the island’s resonant surface rather than describing the
island’s helical phase or radial extent.

At the island center, the normalized toroidal-flux coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}} = \left(\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}\right)^{1/2}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is the normalized toroidal-flux coordinate,
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the enclosed toroidal magnetic flux at the island
center, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}$ is its value at the magnetic axis, and
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}}$ is its value at the equilibrium boundary.

The quantity applies to the center, or resonant-surface location, of one
specified neoclassical tearing-mode island and is a pointwise
magnetic-surface label, not an average over the island or a sum over modes.
It is not a cylindrical radial distance, a local vector component, or the
unnormalized toroidal-flux radius represented by [toroidal flux coordinate
at the neoclassical tearing-mode
center](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode_center).

It is the locus-specific evaluation of the parent [normalized toroidal flux
coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate) at the neoclassical
tearing-mode center. The island’s helical orientation is described
separately by its [neoclassical tearing-mode
phase](name:neoclassical_tearing_mode_phase).

items.name: total_neutral_number_density
items.description:
Total neutral number density is the local abundance per physical volume of
one selected neutral species, combining thermal and nonthermal populations
summed over all charge states. It counts particles rather than weighting
them by charge, mass, or energy.
items.documentation:
Total neutral number density is the local abundance per physical volume of
one selected neutral species, combining its thermal and nonthermal particle
populations. It counts particles rather than weighting them by charge, mass,
or energy.

For species $s$ at position $\mathbf{r}$, the total is:

$$
n_s^0(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_q \left[n_{s,q,\mathrm{th}}^0(\mathbf{r}) + n_{s,q,\mathrm{nth}}^0(\mathbf{r})\right]
$$

where $n_s^0$ is the total neutral number density, $s$ labels the selected
neutral species, the superscript $0$ identifies the neutral population,
$\mathbf{r}$ is spatial position, and $q$ labels charge state. The terms
$n_{s,q,\mathrm{th}}^0$ and $n_{s,q,\mathrm{nth}}^0$ are the thermal and
nonthermal number-density contributions, respectively, for species $s$ and
charge state $q$.

The quantity is local at a plasma position, including core and edge or
scrape-off-layer regions as applicable; it is not integrated or averaged
over a spatial region. It applies to one selected species: thermal and
nonthermal contributions are summed over all charge states, but distinct
species are not combined. It is not a charge-, mass-, or energy-weighted
density.

The [fast neutral internal-state number
density](name:fast_neutral_internal_state_number_density) is narrower,
applying to fast neutral particles in one specified internal state rather
than defining the full thermal-plus-nonthermal, charge-state-summed
quantity. The [total ion number density](name:total_ion_number_density) is
the corresponding total particle number density for an ion species.

items.name: spectral_etendue_of_soft_xray_detector
items.description:
Response-weighted optical phase-space acceptance of a spectrometer channel,
combining collecting area and accepted ray directions across its wavelength
response.
items.documentation:
Spectral étendue is the optical phase-space acceptance of one spectrometer
channel after weighting its wavelength-dependent collecting area and
accepted ray directions by the channel response. It represents
response-weighted optical throughput rather than a wavelength interval or a
calibration coefficient.

The response-weighted étendue is defined by

$$
\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{spec}} = \int w(\lambda)\,A_{\mathrm{eff}}(\lambda)\,\Omega_{\mathrm{acc}}(\lambda)\,d\lambda
$$

where $\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{spec}}$ is the spectral étendue, $w(\lambda)$ is
the normalized wavelength-response weighting, $\lambda$ is wavelength,
$A_{\mathrm{eff}}(\lambda)$ is the effective collecting area, and
$\Omega_{\mathrm{acc}}(\lambda)$ is the accepted solid angle. The weighting
satisfies $\int w(\lambda)\,d\lambda = 1$.

The quantity applies to radiation admitted by the specified spectrometer
channel over its wavelength-response domain. It aggregates aperture
acceptance, ray-direction acceptance, and wavelength response; it does not
describe a particular plasma population or define a spatial emission region.

It specializes the geometric acceptance represented by
etendue_of_spectrometer_channel by incorporating spectral weighting. It is
distinct from
[effective_spectral_width_of_spectrometer_channel](name:effective_spectral_width_of_spectrometer_channel),
which represents a response-equivalent wavelength interval, and from
[spectral_calibration_factor_of_spectrometer_channel](name:spectral_calibration_factor_of_spectrometer_channel),
which scales an instrument response to detector count rate.

items.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part
items.description:
Radial perturbed plasma magnetic field real part is the in-phase radial
component of the complex first-order plasma magnetic-field perturbation for
one toroidal Fourier harmonic. The radial direction is the R component in
the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Radial perturbed plasma magnetic field real part is the real part of the
cylindrical radial component of a complex first-order plasma magnetic-field
perturbation for a selected toroidal Fourier harmonic. The radial direction
is the $+\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ basis direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

The defining component is

$$
\delta B_{R,n}^{\mathrm{re}} = \operatorname{Re}\!\left(\widetilde{\delta\mathbf{B}}_n \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}\right)
$$

where $\delta B_{R,n}^{\mathrm{re}}$ is this real component,
$\widetilde{\delta\mathbf{B}}_n$ is the complex first-order plasma
magnetic-field perturbation for toroidal Fourier mode number $n$,
$\operatorname{Re}$ takes the real part, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the
radial basis vector.

Together with [radial perturbed plasma magnetic field imaginary
part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part), it
determines the complex [radial perturbed plasma magnetic
field](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field); changing the chosen
complex phase of the harmonic rotates the real and imaginary parts without
changing the represented perturbation. It is the radial component
counterpart of [toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic
field](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field) and is distinct from a
flux-surface-normal projection, which would use a unit normal to a specified
flux coordinate rather than $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$.

Sign convention: Positive when the in-phase radial perturbation component
points in the $+\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ direction of increasing major radius $R$.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_major_radius
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged magnetic-geometry coefficient measuring the squared
toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient relative to the squared major radius.
items.documentation:
This quantity is a magnetic-geometry metric coefficient that characterizes
how a toroidal-flux radial coordinate varies across nested magnetic
surfaces, with the variation weighted by inverse squared major radius.

It is defined by

$$
g_2 = \left\langle \frac{|\nabla \rho|^2}{R^2} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $g_2$ is the flux-surface-averaged metric coefficient, $\rho$ is the
toroidal-flux radial coordinate, $\nabla\rho$ is its spatial gradient,
$|\nabla\rho|$ is the gradient magnitude, $R$ is the major radius, and the
subscript $\mathrm{FS}$ denotes the prescribed average over a complete
magnetic flux surface.

The quantity applies to an equilibrium magnetic flux surface and represents
an aggregate over that surface rather than a pointwise local value. It has
no species, population, or transport-channel restriction.

It is the flux-surface average of the local ratio defined by [ratio of
square of toroidal flux coordinate gradient magnitude to square of major
radius](name:ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_major_radius).
Unlike [flux-surface-averaged square of toroidal flux coordinate gradient
magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude),
it retains the inverse-square-major-radius weighting; the numerator is
constructed from the [toroidal flux coordinate gradient
magnitude](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude).

items.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the density-normalized
poloidal diffusive thermal-energy flux of one ion charge state to its local
temperature gradient.
items.documentation:
The ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient in the poloidal direction
quantifies gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by
ions in one specified charge state. It is the poloidal directional
specialization of the [ion charge-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and
excludes convective, advective, and other nondiffusive contributions.

The defining relation for the density-normalized poloidal diffusive energy
flux is:

$$
\frac{Q_{i,z,\mathrm{diff}}^{\mathrm{pol}}}{n_{i,z}} = -D_{i,z,E}^{\mathrm{pol}}\,\nabla_{\mathrm{pol}} T_{i,z}
$$

where $Q_{i,z,\mathrm{diff}}^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal component of
the diffusive thermal-energy flux, $n_{i,z}$ is the number density of ion
charge state $z$, $T_{i,z}$ is its temperature, and
$\nabla_{\mathrm{pol}}T_{i,z}$ is the poloidal component of its local
temperature gradient.

This coefficient applies to one specified charge state and is not aggregated
over charge states. It is distinct from the ion-level [poloidal ion energy
diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and
the broader [poloidal total ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_total_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

items.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective velocity coefficient for advective, non-diffusive transport of
momentum carried by a specified ion species and charge state, distinct from
its bulk flow velocity.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing the advective,
non-diffusive transport of momentum for a specified ion species and charge
state. It is a transport closure quantity, not the actual bulk flow velocity
of that ion charge state.

For each selected momentum component and transport direction, the convective
momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{conv}} = V_{\mathrm{conv}} P
$$

where $\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the corresponding convective momentum
flux, $V_{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the momentum convection velocity, and $P$ is
the corresponding momentum density. The generic momentum convection velocity
uses the same closure relation across momentum populations.

This charge-state-resolved quantity applies to one ion charge state and
excludes summation over other charge states. Its vector may be resolved into
radial, poloidal, toroidal, vertical, or field-aligned components; unlike
energy convection velocity, it transports momentum rather than energy. It is
distinct from the ion charge state's material flow velocity.

Sign convention: Positive when the associated convective momentum flux is in
the chosen positive transport direction for positive transported momentum
density.

items.name: parallel_total_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Parallel diffusion coefficient for total ion energy transport is the
effective scalar diffusivity in a Fickian flux-gradient closure along the
magnetic-field direction, with total ion energy summed over all ion species
and charge states.
items.documentation:
Parallel diffusion coefficient for total ion energy transport is the
effective scalar diffusivity that multiplies the parallel gradient of total
ion energy density in a Fickian closure. It is the parallel component of the
[total ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:total_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient), where total ion
energy is summed over all ion species and charge states.

A local diffusive closure for the parallel total-ion-energy flux is

$$
q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{i,\parallel} = -D^{E_i}_{\parallel}\,\nabla_{\parallel} W^{\mathrm{tot}}_i
$$

where $q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{i,\parallel}$ is the diffusive flux of total ion
energy along the magnetic-field direction, $D^{E_i}_{\parallel}$ is this
coefficient, $\nabla_{\parallel} = \hat{b}\cdot\nabla$ is the derivative
along the magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{b}$, and $W^{\mathrm{tot}}_i$ is
the total ion energy density summed over all ion species and charge states.

This coefficient represents only the diffusive parallel contribution;
advective, convective, source, sink, and cross-field transport terms are
outside its definition. It is directionally distinct from the [poloidal
total ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_total_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

Sign convention: Positive when the diffusive total-ion-energy flux is
directed down the parallel gradient of total ion energy density.

items.name: radial_outline_of_iron_core_segment
items.description:
Non-negative major-radius coordinate of a point on an iron-core segment
cross-sectional outline in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame,
where R is measured away from the symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Non-negative major-radius coordinate of a point on an iron-core segment
cross-sectional outline is the distance of that point from the toroidal
symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$
is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It
identifies the radial location of an outline point; increasing $R$ is
directed away from the symmetry axis along $+\hat{R}$.

For a point whose position perpendicular to the symmetry axis is described
in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis with
$\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$, the coordinate is

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the Cartesian coordinates in the plane normal to the
symmetry axis.

The quantity applies only to the outline locus of the iron-core segment. It
is distinct from the [radial coordinate of an arc-of-circle
center](name:radial_coordinate_of_arc_of_circle_center), which locates a
geometry-defining center rather than the radial coordinate of each outline
point.

items.name: greenwald_density
items.description:
Greenwald density is the empirical electron number-density limit associated
with a confined plasma, set by the magnitude of plasma current and the
effective minor radius. It is the density reference used by Greenwald
fractions, not the fraction itself.
items.documentation:
Greenwald density is the empirical electron number-density limit associated
with a confined toroidal plasma. It is a global density reference for
proximity-to-limit quantities, not a measured local or averaged electron
density.

The Greenwald density is defined by scaling the magnitude of the plasma
current by the plasma cross-sectional area represented through the effective
minor radius:

$$
n_G = C_G \frac{\left|I_p\right|}{\pi a_\mathrm{eff}^2}
$$

where $n_G$ is the Greenwald density, $C_G$ is the Greenwald proportionality
constant, $I_p$ is the [plasma current](name:plasma_current), and
$a_\mathrm{eff}$ is the effective minor radius of the confined plasma
cross-section.

This quantity denotes the empirical limit density itself. It does not denote
a local electron density, a line-averaged electron density, a
volume-averaged electron density, or any normalized Greenwald fraction.

For Greenwald-fraction quantities, this density is the common denominator:
the [ratio of line-averaged electron density to Greenwald
density](name:ratio_of_line_averaged_electron_density_to_greenwald_density)
divides a specified line-averaged electron-density measure by $n_G$.

items.name: ion_species_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
items.description:
Number flux density of ions from a selected species emitted by a
plasma-facing wall through surface-emission processes, summed over all
ionization states and directed into the plasma.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local rate at which ions of one selected species leave
a plasma-facing wall through surface-emission processes, expressed per unit
wall area. It represents the emitted component of particle exchange rather
than the total or net ion exchange at the wall.

The local emitted particle flux density is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{em}} = \frac{dN_{i,\mathrm{em}}}{dA\,dt}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{em}}$ is the emitted ion particle flux density,
$N_{i,\mathrm{em}}$ is the number of emitted ions of the selected species,
$A$ is wall surface area, $t$ is time, the subscript $i$ identifies the
selected ion species, and the subscript $\mathrm{em}$ identifies the
surface-emission contribution.

The quantity applies locally at a plasma-facing wall and is summed over all
positive ionization states of the selected species. It excludes neutral
particles and has no spatial maximum, surface integral, or spatial average
over the wall.

Unlike the [ion charge-state particle flux at the
wall](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux_at_wall), which describes ions
incident on the wall in a specified charge state, this quantity describes
ions leaving the wall and is not the net difference between incident and
emitted flux. The corresponding emitted-electron quantity, [electron
particle flux at the wall due to surface
emission](name:electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission),
applies the same wall-local process distinction to electrons.

items.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis is the signed equilibrium flux
through a horizontal disk bounded by the toroidal circle at that location.
items.documentation:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis is the signed equilibrium flux
through a horizontal disk centered on the toroidal symmetry axis and bounded
by the toroidal circle at that location. It is the magnetic-axis value of
[poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux), a component-specific
specialization of [magnetic flux](name:magnetic_flux).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the defining
flux is

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{p},\mathrm{axis}} = 2\pi \int_0^{R_{\mathrm{axis}}} B_Z(R', Z_{\mathrm{axis}})\,R'\,dR'
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{p},\mathrm{axis}}$ is the poloidal magnetic flux at the
magnetic axis, $R_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is its major radius, $Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$
is its [vertical coordinate](name:vertical_coordinate_of_magnetic_axis),
$B_Z$ is the vertical component of the total equilibrium magnetic field, and
$R'$ is the integration coordinate along major radius.

The value includes both plasma-generated and externally generated
equilibrium flux, rather than only [external magnetic
flux](name:external_magnetic_flux). It is neither an axis-to-boundary flux
difference nor a normalized flux label, and it need not vanish at the
magnetic axis.

Together with the [poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma
boundary](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary), denoted by
$\Phi_{\mathrm{p},b}$, it defines the normalized flux fraction $f =
(\Phi_{\mathrm{p}}-\Phi_{\mathrm{p},\mathrm{axis}})/(\Phi_{\mathrm{p},b}-\Phi_{\mathrm{p},\mathrm{axis}})$,
where $\Phi_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the equilibrium poloidal flux at the evaluation
location and the denominator must be nonzero. This fraction supplies the
reference for the [normalized poloidal flux
coordinate](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate), with zero at the
magnetic axis and unity at the plasma boundary. These reference values
remain applicable when the region being described does not extend to either
endpoint.

Sign convention: Positive when the net vertical magnetic flux through the
defining disk is directed toward increasing $Z$.

The closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux
surfaces are arranged. Where $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}(R_{\mathrm{axis}},
Z_{\mathrm{axis}}) = 0$, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is poloidal magnetic
field; $R_{\mathrm{axis}}, Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the O-point inside the
nested closed flux surfaces.

items.name: upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Upper-inner squareness of the plasma boundary is the dimensionless Luce
shape coefficient measuring the upper high-field-side corner’s signed
departure from a reference ellipse.
items.documentation:
The upper-inner squareness of the plasma boundary is the dimensionless Luce
shape coefficient quantifying the departure of the upper inboard corner of
the last closed flux surface from a reference ellipse. It is the
upper-quadrant component of the [inner squareness of the plasma
boundary](name:inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary), paired with the
[lower-inner squareness of the plasma
boundary](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary).

In a poloidal cross-section at fixed toroidal angle $\phi$ of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the coefficient is

$$
\zeta_{\mathrm{UI}} = \frac{\overline{OD} - \overline{OE}}{\overline{OF} - \overline{OE}}
$$

where $O$ is the reference-ellipse center, $D$ is the upper-inner boundary
intersection along the corner diagonal, $E$ is the corresponding ellipse
intersection, and $F$ is the corner of the circumscribing rectangle. The
reference ellipse is determined by the boundary size and shaping parameters.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_detector
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of the detector center in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, locating the detector relative to the toroidal
symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Radial coordinate of a detector is the major-radius coordinate of the
detector center in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. In
this frame, $R$ is major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above
$+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The detector-center radial coordinate is related to Cartesian coordinates of
the same point by

$$
R_d = \sqrt{x_d^2 + y_d^2}
$$

where $R_d$ is the radial coordinate of the detector center, and $x_d$ and
$y_d$ are the detector-center Cartesian coordinates in the right-handed
Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame with origin on the toroidal
symmetry axis and $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$ vertical.

The scope is the detector as a whole, and the reference point is its center.
This is a point coordinate, not an area average over the detector surface,
not an average over detector pixels, and not the coordinate of an
alternative detector-plane origin.

This quantity is a detector-specific specialization of [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate): it applies the same major-radius
coordinate to the detector center. It is distinct from the [radial
coordinate of detector pixel](name:radial_coordinate_of_detector_pixel),
which applies to an individual pixel center, and from the [radial coordinate
of diagnostic aperture](name:radial_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture),
which applies to an aperture reference point.

items.name: difference_of_total_plasma_heating_power_and_time_derivative_of_plasma_stored_energy
items.description:
Instantaneous plasma power available for confinement losses after correcting
total coupled heating for the rate of change of stored plasma energy.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the instantaneous global power-balance residual available
to account for energy leaving the plasma confinement system. It corrects the
total plasma heating power for transient changes in the plasma’s stored
energy.

It is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{loss}} = P_{\mathrm{heat,total}} - \frac{dW_{\mathrm{plasma}}}{dt}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{loss}}$ is the power-balance residual represented by this
quantity, $P_{\mathrm{heat,total}}$ is the total plasma heating power,
$W_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the total stored energy of the plasma, and $t$ is
time.

The quantity is global and aggregated over all heating contributions
included in total plasma heating power and over the complete stored
plasma-energy reservoir. It is not the heating input itself, a single-source
heating contribution, or a regional radiation measurement; [radiated power
over the core region](name:radiated_power_over_core_region) is a specific
loss channel rather than this balance residual. A positive value means
heating exceeds the instantaneous increase in stored energy, while a
negative value means stored energy is increasing faster than the heating
input.

This residual is the loss-power term in the conventional energy-confinement
relation $\tau_E = W_{\mathrm{plasma}}/P_{\mathrm{loss}}$, where $\tau_E$ is
the energy confinement time; transient storage changes are therefore
excluded from the inferred loss power rather than counted as losses.

items.name: total_ion_energy_flux
items.description:
Total ion energy flux is the local ion energy-flux-density vector carried by
all ion species and charge states, including conductive thermal-energy
transport and convective enthalpy or bulk-kinetic transport.
items.documentation:
Total ion energy flux is the local energy-flux-density vector carried by all
ion species and charge states. It represents the rate at which the aggregate
ion energy reservoir crosses unit oriented area after projection onto the
surface normal, including conductive thermal-energy transport and convective
enthalpy or bulk-kinetic transport when those contributions are in scope.

For a multi-species plasma, the aggregate vector
$\mathbf{Q}_i^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is defined as the sum of conductive and
convective species contributions:

$$
\mathbf{Q}_i^{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_{s \in \mathrm{ions}} \left(\mathbf{q}_{s,\mathrm{cond}} + \mathbf{q}_{s,\mathrm{conv}}\right)
$$

where $s$ indexes ion species and charge states,
$\mathbf{q}_{s,\mathrm{cond}}$ is the conductive heat-flux vector of species
$s$, and $\mathbf{q}_{s,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective energy-flux vector
of species $s$. For an ideal monatomic ion fluid, the enthalpy part of
$\mathbf{q}_{s,\mathrm{conv}}$ is $(5/2)p_s\mathbf{v}_s$, where $p_s$ is
scalar pressure and $\mathbf{v}_s$ is mean flow velocity; bulk-kinetic
convection is included only when macroscopic flow energy belongs to the
selected ion energy reservoir.

As an extensive flux-density quantity, the aggregate is summed over all ion
species and over all charge states of each species; it is not a
density-weighted mean. It is local, not a flux-surface average or
area-integrated power. Projection onto an oriented surface normal gives a
scalar [ion_energy_flux](name:ion_energy_flux), and named aggregate
projections include
[radial_total_ion_energy_flux](name:radial_total_ion_energy_flux),
poloidal_total_ion_energy_flux, and
[parallel_total_ion_energy_flux](name:parallel_total_ion_energy_flux). The
quantity is distinct from
[total_thermal_ion_heat_flux](name:total_thermal_ion_heat_flux), which
restricts the transported reservoir to total ion thermal heat, and is an ion
contribution to [total_energy_flux](name:total_thermal_ion_heat_flux).

Sign convention: Positive when a represented component of the vector carries
ion energy in the positive direction of its stated basis vector, projection
direction, or oriented surface normal.

items.name: solid_angle_of_neutron_detector
items.description:
Geometric acceptance of a neutron detector aperture as viewed from a neutron
emission point, independent of detector efficiency and material response.
items.documentation:
The solid angle is the geometric measure of the aperture’s apparent extent
from a neutron emission point. It is nonnegative and depends only on the
aperture geometry, its orientation, and the source-point location; detector
efficiency and converter response are excluded.

For a point source, the solid angle is defined by

$$
\Omega = \int_A \frac{\cos\theta}{r^2}\,dA
$$

where $A$ is the aperture surface, $r$ is the distance from the source point
to an aperture element, and $\theta$ is the angle between the aperture
normal and the line from the source point to that element. For a finite
source region, the quantity denotes the specified volume average of this
point-source solid angle; it does not imply weighting by the neutron
emission profile. The geometric aperture dimensions described by area of
neutron detector and [radius of neutron
detector](name:radius_of_neutron_detector) can determine the acceptance but
do not include detector efficiency, which is a separate quantity described
by [efficiency of neutron
detector](name:spectral_efficiency_of_neutron_detector).

items.name: ion_momentum_diffusivity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Fickian coefficient for flux-surface-normal redistribution of total ion
momentum caused specifically by diamagnetic drift, excluding other transport
mechanisms.
items.documentation:
This diffusivity quantifies the diamagnetic-drift contribution to
cross-field redistribution of ion momentum, with the ion quantity aggregated
over all ionic charge states. It is distinct from the charge-state-resolved
coefficient and from the mechanism-unspecified [ion diamagnetic momentum
diffusivity](name:ion_diamagnetic_momentum_diffusivity).

The Fickian constitutive relation is

$$
\Pi_{i,\mathrm{dia}} = -\rho_i D_{i,\mathrm{mom}}^{\mathrm{dia}} \, \nabla_\perp V_i
$$

where $\Pi_{i,\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic-drift contribution to ion
momentum flux, $\rho_i$ is total ion mass density,
$D_{i,\mathrm{mom}}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is this diffusivity, $\nabla_\perp$ is
the gradient normal to magnetic flux surfaces, and $V_i$ is the
corresponding ion flow-velocity component. The coefficient describes only
the diffusive momentum-transport contribution due to diamagnetic drift;
convective and other mechanism-resolved contributions are excluded. Its
constitutive sign follows the negative-gradient relation, so outward flux
results from an outward-decreasing flow component.

items.name: neon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Particle number density of neon ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned
to an internal transport barrier, summed over ionization states and
excluding neutral neon.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of neon ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned
to an internal transport barrier is the local density of the neon-ion
population at that flux-surface location. Neon has atomic number $Z=10$;
unless a charge state is specified separately, all neon ionization states
are included and neutral neon is excluded.

The number density is defined by

$$
n = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{\Delta N}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n$ is number density, $N$ is the number of counted neon ions, and $V$
is volume. The internal transport barrier is the designated flux-surface
location where reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep density
gradients. This quantity is the neon-specific member of [density at the
internal transport barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier),
analogous to [carbon density at the internal transport
barrier](name:carbon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier).

items.name: second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture
items.description:
Signed coordinate of an individual diagnostic-aperture outline vertex along
the second local tangential direction, measured from the aperture-local
origin.
items.documentation:
The second local tangential coordinate of a diagnostic-aperture outline
vertex is the signed component of the vertex's displacement from the
aperture-local origin along the second local tangential direction. It
applies to each outline vertex individually.

For an outline vertex with position vector $\mathbf{r}_v$, its coordinate is
defined by the projection:

$$
X_2 = (\mathbf{r}_v - \mathbf{r}_0) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_2
$$

where $X_2$ is the second local tangential coordinate, $\mathbf{r}_v$ is the
position vector of the outline vertex, $\mathbf{r}_0$ is the position vector
of the aperture-local origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$ is the unit vector
along the positive second local tangential direction.

Each value describes one vertex, not an average across vertices or an
aperture width; it is a tangential displacement, not a displacement along
the aperture normal. Paired with the [first local tangential coordinate of
the diagnostic aperture] for the same vertex, it specifies that vertex's
position in the outline. Together, the paired coordinates of the outline
vertices define the aperture boundary and its
[area](name:area_of_diagnostic_aperture).

Sign convention: Positive when the vertex displacement from the
aperture-local origin projects along the positive second local tangential
direction.

items.name: vertical_conductivity
items.description:
Local electrical conductivity relating an electric field along the toroidal
symmetry axis to the conductive current density induced in that same
direction.
items.documentation:
Vertical conductivity is the vertical-vertical projection of the local
electrical-conductivity tensor in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis.

The defining tensor projection is:

$$
\sigma_{ZZ} = \hat{\mathbf{z}}\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\sigma_{ZZ}$ is the vertical conductivity, $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is
the [plasma electrical-conductivity
tensor](name:plasma_electrical_conductivity), and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the
unit vector along the symmetry axis toward increasing height. For a purely
vertical electric field, this coefficient gives the induced vertical
conductive current density per applied electric field.

This is a local transport coefficient, not a height coordinate or a
spatially averaged conductivity. Vertical current driven by radial or
toroidal electric fields involves off-diagonal tensor components and is not
included in this coefficient.

[Radial conductivity](name:radial_conductivity) is the corresponding
diagonal projection along the major-radius direction. In contrast, [parallel
conductivity](name:parallel_conductivity) projects along the local magnetic
field rather than the geometric vertical direction.

items.name: ion_momentum_flux
items.description:
