Vector rate of linear momentum transport per unit area for the total ion
population, summed over all ion species and charge states, encompassing
convective, pressure, and viscous stress contributions.
items.documentation:
The ion momentum flux represents the rate at which the total ion population
transports linear momentum through a unit area, summed over all ion species
and charge states. It combines convective bulk-flow momentum, scalar
pressure (isotropic kinetic stress), and viscous or turbulent off-diagonal
stress contributions. Its divergence appears in the ion momentum balance
equation, governing the forces that drive and redistribute plasma rotation
and bulk flows; this quantity is the ion-specific instance of the general
[momentum_flux](name:momentum_flux).

The total ion momentum flux density is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}_\mathrm{ion} = \sum_s \left( m_s n_s \mathbf{v}_s \mathbf{v}_s + p_s \mathbf{I} + \boldsymbol{\pi}_s \right)
$$

where $m_s$ is the ion species mass, $n_s$ is the number density,
$\mathbf{v}_s$ is the mean fluid velocity, $p_s$ is the scalar pressure,
$\mathbf{I}$ is the unit tensor, and $\boldsymbol{\pi}_s$ is the viscous
stress tensor for species $s$, with the sum running over all ion species.

Specific resolved components isolate distinct transport channels:
[toroidal_ion_momentum_flux](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_flux) quantifies the
radial flux of toroidal momentum relevant to rotation drive,
[parallel_ion_momentum_flux](name:parallel_ion_momentum_flux) captures
transport along the magnetic field, and
[poloidal_ion_momentum_flux](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux) resolves the
poloidal channel. The convective contribution can be parameterized through
the radial_ion_momentum_effective_convection_velocity.

Sign convention: Positive when ion momentum is transported in the positive
direction of the resolved projection axis in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with outward (increasing $R$) as positive for radial
projections.

items.name: neutral_diamagnetic_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless factor setting the free-streaming upper bound on flux of a
neutral species’ diamagnetic momentum component in edge-fluid transport
closures.
items.documentation:
The neutral-species diamagnetic momentum flux limiter coefficient scales the
collisionless free-streaming bound on transport of the diamagnetic component
of [momentum](name:momentum) in edge-fluid closures. Flux limiting restricts
the corresponding momentum-flux magnitude without reversing its direction.

The limiting magnitude is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{0,\mathrm{dia}}^{\max} = \alpha_{0,\mathrm{dia}}\Pi_{0,\mathrm{dia}}^{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\alpha_{0,\mathrm{dia}}$ is this nonnegative coefficient,
$\Pi_{0,\mathrm{dia}}^{\max}$ is the maximum permitted momentum-flux
magnitude, and $\Pi_{0,\mathrm{dia}}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the nonnegative
collisionless free-streaming reference magnitude for the same momentum
component. The subscript $0$ denotes the neutral population. This relation
specifies the cap, not a particular interpolation between diffusive and
free-streaming transport.

The coefficient applies to a specified neutral species without selecting an
individual neutral state; it is not a total-plasma coefficient. The
diamagnetic label identifies the transported momentum component, not the
direction in which its flux crosses an oriented surface, and does not imply
a charge-driven diamagnetic drift of neutral particles.

This is the neutral-species specialization of the [diamagnetic momentum flux
limiter coefficient](name:diamagnetic_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).
The [neutral-state diamagnetic momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:neutral_state_diamagnetic_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
instead applies to a specified neutral state; the species-level coefficient
is not defined as a sum of state-resolved coefficients.

items.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_convection_velocity
items.description:
Poloidal component of the effective velocity convecting energy for one ion
charge state along the poloidal direction of flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective poloidal convection velocity for the energy
carried by one specified ion charge state. It is the poloidal component of
the ion charge-state energy convection velocity, representing advective
rather than diffusive energy transport.

The poloidal convective energy flux is defined by

$$
\mathcal{F}_{E,i,q}^{\theta,\mathrm{conv}} = v_{E,i,q}^{\theta}\,\mathcal{E}_{i,q}
$$

where $\mathcal{F}_{E,i,q}^{\theta,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the poloidal
convective energy flux, $v_{E,i,q}^{\theta}$ is this effective velocity,
$\mathcal{E}_{i,q}$ is the energy density of ion charge state $q$, and $i$
identifies the ion species. The component is expressed in flux coordinates
$(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, with $\theta$ the poloidal coordinate.

This quantity is distinct from the particle-transport velocity [poloidal ion
charge-state convection
velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity) and from the
energy diffusivity [poloidal ion charge-state energy
diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity).

Sign convention: Positive when the associated convective energy flux is
directed toward increasing poloidal coordinate $\theta$.

items.name: particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
items.description:
Particle number flux emanating from a plasma-facing wall surface through
surface-emission processes and directed from the wall material into the
plasma.
items.documentation:
Particle number flux emanating from a plasma-facing wall surface through
surface-emission processes is the surface-normal rate density of particles
generated by the wall material and carried into the plasma.

The emitted particle flux density is defined by:

$$
F_N^{\mathrm{emit}} = \frac{\mathrm{d}N_{\mathrm{emit}}}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $F_N^{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the emitted particle-number flux density,
$N_{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the number of particles emitted, $A$ is emitting wall
area, and $t$ is time.

This quantity applies to emitted electrons, selected ion species, and
neutral particles. For an ion-species quantity, the particle number is
summed over all ionization states; the parent does not require summation
across distinct particle species. It is a local flux density per wall area,
not a total emission rate integrated over the wall, and excludes particles
incident on the wall and the resulting net wall flux.

This is the particle-number specialization of
[flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission)
and is the common abstraction for
[electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission),
[ion_species_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:ion_species_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission),
and
[neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission).
Unlike
[energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission),
it counts emitted particles rather than the energy they carry.

Sign convention: Positive when the emitted particle flux is directed from
the wall material into the plasma.

items.name: second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_soft_xray_detector
items.description:
Signed coordinate of a soft X-ray detector outline vertex along the second
local tangential (X2) axis of the detector-local right-handed Cartesian
frame.
items.documentation:
The second local tangential coordinate $x_2$ locates a vertex of the soft
X-ray detector outline along the X2 axis of the detector-local frame. In
this right-handed Cartesian triad, X3 is the detector's outward
plasma-facing surface normal, X1 is the first local tangential axis directed
more horizontally toward the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$,
and X2 = X3 $\times$ X1 completes the right-handed triad. The ordered set of
$(x_1, x_2)$ vertex pairs defines the detector boundary polygon in the X1–X2
plane; $x_1$ is given by [first local tangential
coordinate](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_soft_xray_detector).
Together the two tangential coordinates fully specify the detector aperture
geometry in the object-local frame, distinct from the aperture outline given
by [second local tangential coordinate of a diagnostic
aperture](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture).

items.name: runaway_electron_kinetic_energy
items.description:
Relativistic kinetic energy summed over the entire runaway-electron
population, giving the total energy carried by runaway electrons.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the total kinetic energy carried by all electrons
classified as runaway, integrated over the complete population and its
occupied plasma volume. It excludes electron rest-mass energy and energy
carried by non-runaway populations.

The total energy is defined from the runaway-electron distribution function
by

$$
E_{\mathrm{RE}} = \int_V \int \left[\gamma(\mathbf{p})-1\right]m_e c^2 f_{\mathrm{RE}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{p})\,d^3p\,d^3x
$$

where $E_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the total kinetic energy in J, $V$ is the plasma
volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is position in m, $\mathbf{p}$ is electron momentum in
kg m s$^{-1}$, $m_e$ is the electron rest mass, $c$ is the speed of light,
$f_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the runaway-electron phase-space number distribution,
and $\gamma(\mathbf{p})=\sqrt{1+p^2/(m_e^2c^2)}$ is the Lorentz factor. The
corresponding local density is [runaway electron energy
density](name:runaway_electron_kinetic_energy_density), while volume
averaging gives [volume-averaged runaway electron kinetic energy
density](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_kinetic_energy_density).

items.name: diamagnetic_energy
items.description:
Diamagnetic energy is three-halves of the plasma-volume integral of total
pressure perpendicular to the local magnetic field, including thermal and
fast-particle contributions.
items.documentation:
Diamagnetic energy is a global plasma stored-energy measure defined by the
total pressure perpendicular to the local magnetic field. It includes both
thermal and fast-particle contributions.

The defining relation is:

$$
W_{\mathrm{dia}} = \frac{3}{2}\int_{V_{\mathrm{p}}} p_\perp\,dV
$$

where $W_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic energy, $V_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the
plasma volume, $p_\perp$ is the total perpendicular pressure, and $dV$ is
the physical volume element. Perpendicular pressure is the mean of the two
pressure-tensor components perpendicular to the local magnetic field, summed
over electron and ion species, charge states, and thermal and fast-particle
populations.

This quantity is a volume-integrated pressure measure, not magnetic-field
energy or a thermal-only energy. The population described by [fast-particle
energy](name:fast_particle_energy) contributes through its perpendicular
pressure rather than necessarily through its full kinetic energy. For
nonrelativistic isotropic populations, diamagnetic energy equals their total
random kinetic energy; this equality does not hold generally for anisotropic
populations. Comparison with MHD stored energy requires consistent pressure
and population conventions.

The [time derivative of diamagnetic
energy](name:time_derivative_of_diamagnetic_energy) is the rate of change of
this stored-energy measure, rather than an additional energy contribution.

items.name: deuterium_deuterium_power_density_due_to_fusion
items.description:
Local volumetric power density from deuterium-deuterium thermonuclear
reactions, including energy carried by both the neutron-producing and
proton-producing branches and characterized by their branch-weighted
per-reaction Q value.
items.documentation:
The D-D fusion power density is the local rate at which deuterium-deuterium
thermonuclear reactions $D + D \rightarrow {}^3\mathrm{He} + n$ and $D + D
\rightarrow T + p$ release energy per unit plasma volume. It includes both
the neutron-producing branch and the proton-producing branch, so it
represents branch-summed D-D fusion energy release rather than only
neutron-branch energy.

For a thermal deuterium population, the branch-summed power density is

$$
P_{\mathrm{DD}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{2} n_D(\mathbf{x})^2 \left[\langle\sigma v\rangle_n Q_n + \langle\sigma v\rangle_p Q_p\right]
$$

where $n_D$ is the deuterium ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $\langle\sigma
v\rangle_n$ and $\langle\sigma v\rangle_p$ are the thermonuclear rate
coefficients in m$^3$ s$^{-1}$ for the helium-3-neutron and tritium-proton
branches, $Q_n$ and $Q_p$ are the corresponding branch energies in joules,
and the factor $1/2$ avoids double counting identical deuteron pairs. The
branch Q-values are $Q_n = 3.27\,\mathrm{MeV}$ for $D + D \rightarrow
{}^3\mathrm{He} + n$ and $Q_p = 4.03\,\mathrm{MeV}$ for $D + D \rightarrow T
+ p$; equal branch probabilities give a branch-weighted $Q_{\mathrm{DD}}
\simeq 3.65\,\mathrm{MeV}$ per D-D reaction, to be converted to joules in
the equation.

The displayed expression is the thermal-thermal specialization of the
definition. For beam-thermal, beam-beam, or otherwise non-Maxwellian
deuteron populations, $P_{\mathrm{DD}}$ is still the branch-summed local
energy-release rate, with each branch reaction-rate density multiplied by
its branch energy rather than using Maxwellian rate coefficients. This
quantity is the D-D channel instance of [fusion power
density](name:power_density_due_to_fusion); it includes neutron and
charged-particle product energy and is distinct from fusion neutron
emissivity, from deposited heating of fusion products, and from [D-T fusion
power density](name:deuterium_tritium_power_density_due_to_fusion).

items.name: helium_4_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate of helium-4 delivered to the
plasma vessel by gas injection, with each helium-4 atom contributing two
equivalent-electron counts.
items.documentation:
The helium-4 source rate due to gas injection characterizes the
instantaneous rate at which neutral helium-4 is admitted to the plasma
vessel by gas-injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count
rate. Each helium-4 atom contributes two counts because helium has atomic
number 2.

The defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{He4}} = Z_{\mathrm{He}}\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He4}} = 2\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He4}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the helium-4 atom delivery rate in atoms per
second, and $Z_{\mathrm{He}}=2$ is helium's atomic number. This is the
helium-4 component of the [source rate due to gas
injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection); integrating it over time
gives the [accumulated helium-4 count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection). The
[helium-3 source rate due to gas
injection](name:helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) uses the same
atomic-number weighting but represents a separate isotope inventory.

Sign convention: Positive when helium-4 gas is delivered into the vessel,
increasing the equivalent-electron particle inventory.

items.name: voltage_of_shunt
items.description:
Signed terminal-potential difference across a resistive shunt, providing the
voltage used with its resistance to determine current in an associated
structure segment.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the signed electrical potential difference between the two
terminals of a shunt resistor. It applies to the shunt element associated
with a divertor or vessel structure segment, rather than to an individual
terminal potential or a voltage across another circuit element.

The defining terminal difference is

$$
V_{\mathrm{shunt}} = V_{\mathrm{first}} - V_{\mathrm{second}}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{shunt}}$ is the shunt terminal voltage,
$V_{\mathrm{first}}$ is the electric potential of the first terminal, and
$V_{\mathrm{second}}$ is the electric potential of the second terminal.

The quantity is a direct terminal difference, with no spatial averaging or
charge-state aggregation. For an ohmic shunt, the associated
structure-segment current $I_{\mathrm{shunt}}$ is related to this voltage
and the [resistance of the shunt](name:resistance_of_shunt),
$R_{\mathrm{shunt}}$, by $I_{\mathrm{shunt}} =
V_{\mathrm{shunt}}/R_{\mathrm{shunt}}$. It does not itself represent the
current or the shunt resistance.

Sign convention: Positive when the electric potential of the first shunt
terminal exceeds that of the second shunt terminal.

items.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity
items.description:
Ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the Fick's-law coefficient relating
diffusive momentum flux to the negative gradient of momentum density for a
specified ion charge state.
items.documentation:
Ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the proportionality coefficient
between the diffusive momentum flux of a specified ion charge state and the
negative local gradient of its momentum density, following a Fick's-law
closure for the fluid momentum balance. It describes directional
redistribution of momentum for that charge state.

For transport direction $i$, the diffusive momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{m,i}^{(q)} = -D_{m,i}^{(q)} \frac{\partial\left(\rho_q u_i^{(q)}\right)}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\Gamma_{m,i}^{(q)}$ is the diffusive momentum flux, $D_{m,i}^{(q)}$
is the corresponding momentum diffusivity, $\rho_q$ is the mass density of
the specified ion charge state, $u_i^{(q)}$ is its flow-velocity component,
and $x_i$ is the coordinate along the transport direction.

The quantity is general over directional projections, including the
cross-flux-surface form represented by [radial ion charge-state momentum
diffusivity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity) and the
field-aligned form represented by [parallel ion charge-state momentum
diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity). It is
resolved for one ion charge state rather than summed over charge states as
in ion momentum diffusivity, and is a charge-state-specific instance of
[momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity).

items.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential_real_part
items.description:
Real-valued poloidal component of the perturbed plasma
magnetic-vector-potential eigenfunction for a specified toroidal mode in
linear MHD stability analysis.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the real-valued poloidal component of the perturbed plasma
magnetic vector-potential eigenfunction associated with one toroidal mode of
a linear MHD perturbation.

$$
A_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{real}} = \operatorname{Re}\!\left(\widetilde{A}_{\mathrm{pol}}\right)
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{real}}$ is the real poloidal component,
$\widetilde{A}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the complex poloidal component of the
perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential, and $\operatorname{Re}$ is the
real-part operator.

The quantity applies to the confined plasma contribution for a specified
toroidal mode and retains only the poloidal component and real part of the
complex eigenfunction. It is not the full perturbed vector potential, its
imaginary component, a magnitude, or a component of the perturbed magnetic
field.

The parent [poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential)
contains the corresponding complex poloidal component before real-part
extraction. The real and imaginary components together represent the complex
eigenfunction amplitude; the perturbed magnetic field is obtained from the
curl of the full perturbed vector potential rather than from this component
alone.

Sign convention: Positive when the real component points along the positive
poloidal basis direction used to define $\widetilde{A}_{\mathrm{pol}}$.

items.name: parallel_edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity
items.description:
Kinematic coefficient relating the diffusive flux of field-parallel
edge-plasma bulk momentum to the opposing velocity gradient along the
magnetic field.
items.documentation:
Parallel edge-plasma momentum diffusivity is the kinematic transport
coefficient governing field-aligned diffusion of the parallel component of
aggregate plasma bulk-flow [momentum](name:momentum). It applies to the
plasma population in the edge region, rather than to an individual ion
species or charge state.

In a local velocity-gradient closure, the field-parallel diffusive momentum
flux is:

$$
\Pi_{\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -\rho_m\chi_{\parallel}\frac{\partial v_{\parallel}}{\partial \ell_{\parallel}}
$$

where $\Pi_{\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the flux of parallel bulk-flow
momentum along the magnetic field, $\rho_m$ is the aggregate plasma mass
density, $\chi_{\parallel}$ is this diffusivity, $v_{\parallel}$ is the
projection of the plasma [center-of-mass
velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity) along the local magnetic field, and
$\ell_{\parallel}$ is arc length increasing along that field.

The aggregate momentum and mass density include the charged constituent
species and their charge states; the bulk velocity is their
mass-density-weighted mean. Neutral momentum is excluded. This coefficient
describes diffusive transport, not advective momentum transport, residual
stress, or external momentum sources. The parallel direction follows the
magnetic field and is not a synonym for the toroidal direction or the
flux-surface-normal direction.

This quantity is the field-aligned specialization of [edge-plasma momentum
diffusivity](name:edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity). It has the kinematic
transport role described by [parallel momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), with the
additional restriction to aggregate edge-plasma momentum.

items.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless poloidal ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient
that scales the free-streaming bound on poloidal momentum transport for a
specified ion charge state.
items.documentation:
The poloidal ion charge-state momentum coefficient is a dimensionless
flux-limiter parameter for momentum transport of a specified ion charge
state in the poloidal direction. It is the poloidal component of the vector
quantity [ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

The coefficient $lpha_{s,\box{pol}}$ bounds the poloidal momentum-flux
density through the harmonic-mean combination:

$$
\Pi_{s,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_{s,\mathrm{pol}} \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} \, \Pi_{s,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{diff}}}{|\Pi_{s,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{diff}}| + \alpha_{s,\mathrm{pol}} \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

where $\Pi_{s,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the collisional diffusive
poloidal momentum-flux estimate for charge state $s$, and
$\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} = m_s n_s v_{\mathrm{th},s}^2$ is the free-streaming
reference scale with $m_s$ the ion mass, $n_s$ the charge-state number
density, and $v_{\mathrm{th},s}$ the thermal speed. When
$|\Pi_{s,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{diff}}| \gg \alpha_{s,\mathrm{pol}}
\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$ the flux saturates at
$\pm\alpha_{s,\mathrm{pol}}\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$; otherwise the diffusive
value is recovered unchanged.

The poloidal component is distinct from the [parallel ion charge-state
momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
which projects onto the magnetic-field direction, and from the [toroidal ion
charge-state momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
which applies in the geometric toroidal direction. The coefficient is
intrinsically non-negative; the sign of the limited poloidal momentum flux
is inherited from the reference poloidal momentum-flux estimate.

items.name: radial_total_momentum_flux
items.description:
Radial component of total edge-plasma momentum-flux density, combining
advective, isotropic-pressure, viscous, and turbulent-stress contributions;
radial means the increasing-major-radius R direction in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the radial component of the total edge-plasma momentum-flux
density, representing transport of radial linear momentum rather than stored
momentum or a force source. The radial projection is the component along
$\hat{R}$, the increasing-major-radius direction in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $\phi$ is the toroidal angle and $Z$
is vertical height.

The radial projection of the total momentum-flux tensor through an oriented
surface is:

$$
\Pi_R = \hat{R}\cdot\left(\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{tot}}\cdot\hat{n}\right),
\qquad
\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{tot}} = \rho_{\mathrm{tot}}\,\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{tot}}\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{tot}} + p_{\mathrm{tot}}\,\mathbf{I} + \boldsymbol{\pi}_{\mathrm{tot}}
$$

where $\Pi_R$ is the radial total momentum flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total momentum-flux tensor,
$\hat{n}$ is the unit normal defining the orientation of the crossed
surface, $\rho_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the mass density of the aggregated total
plasma population, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is its bulk flow velocity,
$p_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is its scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ is the identity
tensor, and $\boldsymbol{\pi}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is its viscous or turbulent
stress tensor.

The scope is the total edge-plasma population: contributions from all plasma
species and charge states in that population are summed at the level of
momentum flux, including convective, isotropic-pressure, viscous, and
turbulent-stress terms. It excludes single-species or charge-state-resolved
momentum fluxes, scalar pressure alone, stored momentum density, and force
or torque source densities.

This quantity is the radial projection of [total momentum
flux](name:total_momentum_flux). It uses the same radial coordinate
convention as [radial momentum flux](name:radial_momentum_flux): radial
means increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame, not distance from the magnetic axis and not a flux-surface-normal
projection; [toroidal total momentum
flux](name:toroidal_total_momentum_flux) is the matched toroidal projection
of the same total momentum-flux tensor.

Sign convention: Positive when $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{tot}}\cdot\hat{n}$
has a component in the $+\hat{R}$ direction, toward increasing major radius
$R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: krypton_density_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Number density of the krypton species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for krypton ions at the sheath entrance, summed
over positive ionization states and excluding neutral krypton atoms.
items.documentation:
Number density of the krypton species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for krypton ions at the sheath entrance
immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the
krypton-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local krypton-ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Kr}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Kr}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the krypton-ion number density, $N_{\mathrm{Kr}}$
is the number of krypton ions, and $V$ is the local plasma volume.

This quantity applies to the krypton-ion population immediately adjacent to
a divertor target, evaluated at the plasma-side entrance to the
electrostatic sheath. It is summed over all positive krypton ionization
states, counting each ion once; neutral krypton atoms, electrons, and ions
of other species are excluded.

As a species-specific target-locus quantity, it specializes the broader
[krypton_density](name:krypton_density) by restricting the evaluation point
to the divertor target. Its locus and charge-state aggregation follow the
corresponding
[neon_density_at_divertor_target](name:neon_density_at_divertor_target),
while the species is krypton rather than neon.

items.name: toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Toroidal component of the oxygen impurity ion bulk flow velocity evaluated
at the plasma boundary (last closed flux surface).
items.documentation:
The toroidal velocity of oxygen impurity ions at the plasma boundary
quantifies the toroidal momentum carried by the oxygen ion population at the
last closed flux surface, which separates the magnetically confined plasma
from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. This local point value is
distinct from the flux-surface-averaged quantity
toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary, which
integrates the velocity weighted by the boundary flux-surface geometry.

The toroidal component $v_\phi$ is the projection of the oxygen bulk flow
velocity onto the toroidal direction:

$$
v_\phi = \mathbf{v}_\mathrm{O} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_\mathrm{O}$ is the oxygen ion bulk flow velocity and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal
angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Oxygen toroidal velocity at the boundary is primarily measured by charge
exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS), exploiting the Doppler shift of
oxygen emission lines to extract the ion flow velocity component along
$\hat{\phi}$. Analogous boundary velocities for other impurity species
include
[toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary)
and
[toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

Sign convention: Positive when the oxygen ion flow is directed in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ (counter-clockwise when viewed
from above in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction).

items.name: total_thermal_power_density_due_to_conductive_losses
items.description:
Volumetric rate of thermal plasma energy removal by conductive transport
toward plasma-facing surfaces.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the local volumetric rate at which total thermal plasma
energy is removed by conductive transport toward plasma-facing surfaces. It
represents an aggregate thermal-population loss rather than a
species-resolved contribution, and is distinct from the corresponding
surface energy flux.

$$
P_{\mathrm{cond,loss}} = \nabla \cdot \mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{cond}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{cond,loss}}$ is the conductive-loss power density and
$\mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the total thermal conductive energy-flux
vector. The divergence is taken in physical space; conductive transport is
predominantly parallel to magnetic field lines.

Positive values denote net conductive energy leaving the local plasma
volume. Integrating this density over a volume gives the conductive power
removed from that volume and, when bounded by plasma-facing surfaces,
relates to [power due to conduction](name:power_due_to_conduction).
Radiative, convective, and particle-loss channels are excluded.

items.name: y_direction_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
items.description:
Signed Y-axis projection of the unit vector defining the orientation of an
elliptic shatter cone in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the signed projection of an elliptic shatter cone's
direction unit vector onto the Cartesian Y axis.

The component is defined by

$$
d_y = \hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\rm cone} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{y}}
$$

where $d_y$ is the Y component, $\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\rm cone}$ is the
shatter-cone direction unit vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{y}}$ is the unit
vector along increasing $y$ in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},
\hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis.

This quantity applies only to the shatter-cone direction and represents one
Cartesian component; no population, regional, charge-state, averaging, or
summation convention applies. It is not the direction-vector magnitude and
must not be confused with the [Y component of the shatter-cone major-axis
unit vector](name:y_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), which describes
a geometric axis rather than the cone direction. The complete direction
requires all three Cartesian components.

items.name: power_due_to_fusion
items.description:
Nuclear fusion reaction energy deposition rate integrated over a specified
plasma region or material component. It counts fusion-product energy where
it is deposited, not merely where it is released.
items.documentation:
Nuclear fusion reaction energy deposition rate integrated over a specified
plasma region or material component is the rate at which energy whose
ultimate source is fuel-ion fusion reactions is transferred to matter within
that region or component. It is an extensive deposited-power quantity, so
energy is assigned to the place where it is deposited, which may differ from
the place where the fusion reaction occurred.

For a specified region or component $\Omega$, the quantity is defined by the
local fusion-origin deposition rate density:

$$
P_{\mathrm{fusion,dep}}(\Omega) = \int_{\Omega} q_{\mathrm{fusion,dep}}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{fusion,dep}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local rate density of
energy deposited at position $\mathbf{x}$ by fusion products, fusion-neutron
interactions, and secondary nuclear radiation, and $dV$ is the volume
element of $\Omega$.

Each reaction channel contributes according to the partition of its released
energy among products. For the deuterium-tritium channel, approximately one
fifth of the fusion energy is born in the alpha particle and four fifths in
the neutron; this birth partition does not imply local deposition.
Charged-product energy is included in a plasma region only for the fraction
actually deposited there during slowing down, while escaping charged
products or neutrons contribute where they subsequently deposit energy
through interactions and secondary radiation.

This name is distinct from [power density due to
fusion](name:power_density_due_to_fusion), which denotes local fusion energy
release rate before nonlocal transport, and from neutron power, which tracks
energy carried by neutrons rather than deposited energy in $\Omega$. Power
due to neutron interaction is the neutron-interaction contribution when the
interacting neutrons originate from fusion. The divertor specializations
[deposited power of divertor due to
fusion](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_divertor) and [power of divertor due
to fusion](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_divertor) restrict $\Omega$ to the
divertor; non-fusion heat loads such as conduction, plasma radiation,
charge-exchange neutrals, and externally supplied heating are excluded.

items.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_imaginary_part
items.description:
Quadrature poloidal velocity component of a complex first-order
plasma-velocity perturbation eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier
harmonic. It is the imaginary part of the projection onto the positive
poloidal direction, paired with the in-phase real part.
items.documentation:
Quadrature poloidal velocity component of a complex first-order
plasma-velocity perturbation eigenfunction is the imaginary part of the
poloidal projection of that eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier
harmonic. The poloidal direction is the unit vector $\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta$
toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in a flux-coordinate basis
$(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, with $\phi$ the toroidal angle of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is
vertical height.

The projected component and its imaginary part are defined by

$$
v_{\theta,\mathrm{im}} = \operatorname{Im}\!\left(\tilde v_\theta\right), \qquad \tilde v_\theta = \tilde{\mathbf v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta
$$

where $\tilde{\mathbf v}$ is the complex first-order plasma-velocity
perturbation eigenfunction, $\tilde v_\theta$ is its poloidal component, and
$v_{\theta,\mathrm{im}}$ is the coefficient of the imaginary term when
$\tilde v_\theta = v_{\theta,\mathrm{re}} + i v_{\theta,\mathrm{im}}$.

This quantity is the quadrature component paired with the [poloidal
perturbed plasma velocity real
part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part); together they
specify the complex [poloidal perturbed plasma
velocity](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity) for the chosen harmonic
and phase convention. It is distinct from the corresponding [toroidal
perturbed plasma velocity imaginary
part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_imaginary_part), which
projects the same complex velocity perturbation onto the toroidal direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the quadrature component of $\tilde{\mathbf
v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta$ is aligned with $+\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta$,
toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux-coordinate basis
$(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

items.name: toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Signed toroidal component of the helium-3 ion bulk-flow velocity evaluated
on the plasma boundary, along the direction of increasing toroidal angle.
items.documentation:
The helium-3 ion bulk-flow velocity at the plasma boundary is the
density-weighted mean flow of helium-3 ions over their ion charge states,
evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface, or separatrix. It
describes toroidal motion rather than the full velocity vector.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_{c6,{}^3\mathrm{He}} = \mathbf{u}_{{}^3\mathrm{He}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 ion bulk-flow velocity
and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

Unlike the flux-surface-averaged helium-3 boundary velocity, this quantity
is the velocity evaluated at the plasma boundary and does not imply
flux-surface averaging.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude
items.description:
Flux-surface average of the squared magnitude of the gradient of the
normalized toroidal-flux radius. It is the averaged contravariant radial
metric coefficient for the flux coordinate rho_tor.
items.documentation:
Flux-surface average of the squared magnitude of the gradient of the
toroidal flux coordinate is the average, over one magnetic flux surface, of
the squared norm of $\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}$. It is the
flux-surface-averaged contravariant radial metric coefficient associated
with the radial coordinate in the flux-coordinate system
$(\rho_\mathrm{tor}, \theta, \phi)$, where $\theta$ is a poloidal angle
label and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle.

The quantity is defined by the flux-surface average of the local radial
metric component:

$$
G_{\rho\rho}(\rho_\mathrm{tor}) = \left\langle |\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|^2 \right\rangle_{\rho_\mathrm{tor}} = \frac{\int_{S(\rho_\mathrm{tor})} |\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|^2\, dA / |\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|}{\int_{S(\rho_\mathrm{tor})} dA / |\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|}
$$

where $G_{\rho\rho}$ denotes this flux-surface-averaged metric coefficient,
$\rho_\mathrm{tor}$ is the normalized toroidal-flux radius,
$S(\rho_\mathrm{tor})$ is the magnetic flux surface with that label,
$\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator, $dA$ is the surface-area element,
and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\rho_\mathrm{tor}}$ denotes averaging over that
flux surface.

The coordinate $\rho_\mathrm{tor}$ is constituted by
$\rho_\mathrm{tor}=\sqrt{\Phi/\Phi_b}$, where $\Phi$ is the toroidal
magnetic flux enclosed by the flux surface and $\Phi_b$ is its value at the
plasma boundary. The scope is closed nested equilibrium flux surfaces; the
aggregation convention is an average over the entire surface at fixed
$\rho_\mathrm{tor}$.

This is not the pointwise quantity $|\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|^2$, not the
flux-surface average of $|\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|$, and not a volume or
time average. It belongs to the same flux-surface-averaged geometric-metric
family as the [flux-surface-averaged inverse major
radius](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_major_radius), but it
characterizes the radial metric of the normalized toroidal-flux radius
rather than a major-radius factor.

items.name: first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_bragg_crystal
items.description:
Signed coordinate of a Bragg-crystal outline vertex along the first local
tangential axis of the right-handed crystal-local (e1, e2, e3) frame, with
e1 the more horizontal crystal-tangential direction oriented toward
increasing toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Signed coordinate of a Bragg-crystal outline vertex along the first local
tangential axis is the scalar displacement of that vertex from the
crystal-local reference point along the first in-surface direction of the
Bragg crystal. The quantity is defined in the right-handed crystal-local
$(\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_3)$ frame tied to
the crystal surface.

The coordinate is the projection of the vertex displacement onto the first
local tangential unit vector:

$$
X_1 = (\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}_0) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_1
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector of the Bragg-crystal outline
vertex, $\mathbf{r}_0$ is the position vector of the crystal-local reference
point, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ is the first local tangential unit vector.

The crystal-local triad is fixed geometrically: $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_3$ is the
plasma-facing surface normal, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ is the more horizontal
tangent to the crystal surface and is oriented so that its toroidal
component points in the $+\hat{\phi}$ direction of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2 =
\hat{\mathbf{e}}_3 \times \hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$. This coordinate is distinct
from the [second local tangential
coordinate](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_bragg_crystal), which
uses $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$, and from any coordinate along the surface normal.

Sign convention: Positive when the outline vertex is displaced from the
crystal-local reference point in the $+\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ direction, the
more horizontal crystal-tangential direction oriented toward increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.
